chapters.title: Separating the analogy between the Christians and their books on the Qur’an is an invalid analogy
paragraphs: [Chapter: The analogy of the Christians by their books on the Qur’an is a false analogy]
Then they said: We are amazed at these people, despite their knowledge, intelligence, and knowledge, how they protest against us like this. Saying?

This is also the case when we say and protest against them with this saying that they have changed and altered the book that is in their hands this day. And they wrote in it what they wanted and desired. Were they permissible what we said?
The narrator said about them: So I said to them, “This is what is not permissible, and no one can say it, and it is not possible to change it or replace a single letter.” From him.

They said, Glory be to God the Great! If the book which they have, which is in the same tongue, cannot be altered, nor can one letter of it be changed, how can it be changed? Our Book, which is written in seventy-two languages, and in each language there is such-and-such. He wrote a thousand copies and passed on them until the coming of Muhammad. For more than six hundred years, it has been in the hands of people who read it according to their different languages across the vastness of their countries.

Who spoke with seventy-two tongues? And who is it who ruled over the entire world, its kings, its priests, and its conquerors, until He ruled over all of it in the ends of the earth and gathered them into Four corners of the world until he changes them?

Even if he changed some of them and left others out, this cannot be because they are all one saying and one expression in all tongues. This is something that no one may ever say, and the answer is to say: First:

These words of theirs indicate the utmost ignorance of what the Muslims say in their books, and it turns out that - due to the extent of their ignorance - they think The Muslims say something whose corruption is not hidden from anyone who has the slightest intellect and knowledge, and Muslims, no one among the nations doubts that they The nations with the greatest intellects and understanding, the most complete in knowledge and eloquence, the best in purpose and religion, and the pursuit of truth and justice, and they did not achieve In the human species, there is a nation more perfect than them, and no law is more perfect than the law that their Prophet Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - brought, and he is skilled. Philosophers admit this to them, and that no law has come into the world more perfect than this law.
God has brought together for Muslims all ways and types of human knowledge, for people are of two types: People of the Book and non-People of the Book. Like philosophers and Indians.
Knowledge is acquired through sense and reason, and what is achieved through them and through God’s revelation to His prophets, which is outside of what people share in common. Sense and mind.
For this reason it was said: Scientific methods are sight, consideration, information: sense, reason and revelation: sense, measurement, and prophecy.
The People of the Book were distinguished from others by the prophecy that came to them, while they shared with others the sciences that people shared. Sensory and mental.

The Muslims acquired prophetic and intellectual knowledge that the nations before them did not have, and they were distinguished from them in what the nations did not know. And the mentalities of the nations that reached them, they refined verbally and in meaning until it became better than what they had, and they removed from it falsehood and included It is due to him that they have the advantage over everyone else.

Likewise, God gave them prophetic knowledge that He had not given to any nation before them, and this is clear to those who contemplate the Qur’an along with contemplating the Torah. And the Gospel, for he discovers as a result of the knowledge of the Qur’an something that is not hidden except to the blind.

So how can it be thought that Muslims are aware of the corruption of this speech that these ignorant people thought of them? It is said: Secondly, the answer From several aspects: One of them is that the Muslims did not claim that these books were corrupted after their spread and the large number of copies, but all of them They agree that there has been change and change in many of its meanings and many of its rulings.
This is what all Christians accept in the Torah and the previous prophecies. They accept that the Jews changed many of its meanings. And its provisions.

Among what the Christians accept in their sects is that each group differs from the other in what it interprets the ancient books, and from what the Jews accept that they They agree that Christians interpret the Torah and the prophecies that preceded the Gospel in a way that contradicts their meanings, and that they changed the provisions of the Torah. Changing the meanings of many of the ancient books became agreed upon among Muslims, Jews, and Christians.
As for changing some of its words, there is a dispute among Muslims.
What is correct according to the majority is that he changed some of its words, as was mentioned in his places.

The second aspect: Their analogy is based on their books based on the Qur’an, and just as the call for change is not heard in it, so it is in their books - a false analogy in Its meaning and pronunciation.

As for its meaning: everything upon which the Muslims have unanimously agreed regarding their religion, as a clear consensus and well-known to them, is transmitted from the Messenger in a mutawatir narration. Rather, it is known that it is necessary from his religion, because the five daily prayers, zakat, fasting during the month of Ramadan, the Hajj to the Ancient House, and the obligation of justice. And honesty, and the prohibition of polytheism, immoral acts, and injustice, and even the prohibition of alcohol, gambling, and usury, and other than that, transmitted from the Prophet - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. And peace be upon him - (a frequent transmission, such as the transmission of the words of the Qur’an that indicate this.

From this point of view is the generality of his message - may God bless him and grant him peace - and that he is sent to all people, the People of the Book and non-People of the Book. To the two heavy creatures, mankind and the jinn, and that he used to declare the Jews and Christians as unbelievers who did not follow what God revealed to them, just as he used to declare others among them to be unbelievers. He did not believe in that, and he fought against them and ordered their struggle.

The Muslims have - according to them, narrated frequently from their Prophet - three matters: the wording of the Qur’an and its meanings on which the Muslims have agreed unanimously. The Mutawatir Sunnah is the wisdom that God has revealed to him other than the Qur’an.
As God Almighty said: {Just as We sent among you a messenger from among you, who recites Our verses to you and purifies you and teaches you the Book and the Wisdom} [Al-Baqarah: 151].
And God Almighty said: {And God has sent down to you the Book and the wisdom} [An-Nisa: 113].
And He Almighty said: {And remember the favor of God upon you and what He has sent down to you of the Book and the wisdom} [Al-Baqarah: 231].
And He Almighty said: {And remember what is recited in your homes of the signs of God and wisdom} [Al-Ahzab: 34].

Thus He called Al-Khalil, saying when he and Ishmael built the Kaaba on the land of Paran mentioned in the first book, God Almighty said: {And when Abraham raised the foundations of the House, and Ishmael, “Our Lord, accept it from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.” [Al-Baqarah: 127] (127) {Our Lord, and make us Submitting to you, and from our descendants a nation submissive to you, and show us our rituals, and accept our repentance. Indeed, it is You who are the Accepting, the Merciful.} [Al-Baqarah: 128] (128) {Our Lord, and send Among them is a messenger from among themselves, reciting to them Your verses and teaching them the Book and wisdom and purifying them. Indeed, it is You who is the Mighty, the Wise.} [Al-Baqarah: 129].
And he - may God bless him and grant him peace - said: (Indeed, I have been given the Book and something like it with it.)

Muslims have a mutawatir transmission from their Prophet, with the words of the Qur’an and its agreed-upon meanings, and with the Sunnah mutawatir from him, such as: The noon, afternoon, and evening prayers are four rak’ahs, the sunset prayer is three rak’ahs, and the morning prayer is two rak’ahs, and the same is true for the two evening prayers. And the dawn and the prayers at noon and afternoon, and such as the fact that there are two prostrations in a rak’ah, and the circumambulation of the Kaaba and between Safa and Marwah. Seven pebbles, and throwing seven pebbles at the Jamarat, and the like.

Also, Muslims memorize the Qur’an in their hearts so much that they dispense with the need for copies of the Qur’an, as was proven in the Sahih narrated by Muslim on the authority of the Prophet. - May God’s prayers and peace be upon him - he said, “Indeed, my Lord said to me, ‘Indeed, I have revealed to you a book that cannot be washed away by water, which you can read while asleep and when awake.’”

He says: Even if the Qur’an was washed with water, it would not be washed from the hearts like ancient books, for if there were no copies of them, there would be no one to transfer them. It has been transmitted frequently and preserved in the chests.

The Qur’an is still preserved in the hearts through frequent transmission, even if a disciple wanted to change any part of the Qur’an and presented that to young men. The Muslims would have known that he had changed the Qur’an, because they had memorized the Qur’an without confronting it with a Qur’an, and they denied that.

And the People of the Book, a person among them is able to write many copies of the Torah and the Gospel, and change some of them, and present them to Many of their scholars do not know what has been changed from it unless they show it to the copies they have.
For this reason, when those who abrogated the Torah changed it, it spread among groups of them, and they did not know the change.

(Also, the Muslims have the chains of transmission related to trustworthy narrators transmitting the precise meaning of the religion, as the common people, His Majesty, conveyed, but this is not for the people of The book).

Also, what they mentioned, that their books are written in seventy-two languages, is closer to being changed than a single book in the language. The one; This is what many people protect, and no one can change it.

As for the books written in seventy-two languages, if it is assumed that some of the copies existing in some tongues were changed, some of what was in them The rest of the people of the remaining tongues did not know that, nor did the rest of the people of the other versions know that, as change in them is possible as It is possible in analogues of this.

What they claimed about the impossibility of collecting all the copies is an argument against them, because if that were impossible, it would not be possible to assert that all the copies were in agreement. For one, so that he can attest that they are all in agreement verbally and in meaning, and indeed the possibility of changing them is easier than the possibility of testifying that they are in agreement.

For this reason, it is not possible for anyone to change the Qur’an, despite the fact that it is preserved in hearts and transmitted repeatedly, even though we do not bear witness to all the Qur’an. By agreement, in fact, an error may occur in some copies of the Qur’an that the memorizers of the Qur’an know about, and they do not need to consider that with another Qur’an.

These books are not memorized by any of the people of the Tawātur so that their abrogations can be considered, but since the Prophets - peace be upon them - They were present among them. They were the reference for the people in what they relied on if some people changed any of the books. Then prophecy ceased among them. Change hastened among them.

For this reason, many Christians changed much of the religion of Christ - peace be upon him - shortly after it was raised, and they began to change one thing after another. A group remained among them that adhered to the religion of truth until God sent Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace.

A small group remained of those who followed the true religion, as in the authentic hadith narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, on the authority of Iyad bin Himar. Al-Mujashi’i on the authority of the Prophet that he said: “Indeed, God looked at the people of the earth and detested them, their Arabs and their non-Arabs, except for the remnants of the People of the Book who died.” Before his departure.”

Salman Al-Farisi - who had converted to Christianity after being a Magian - became one group of those who were followers of the religion of Christ - peace be upon him - In Mosul, another in Nisibin, and another in Amuriya.

And each of them told him that only a few people remained following the religion of Christ - peace be upon him - until the last of them told him: No one remained following it. He told him that a prophet of the religion of Abraham would be sent from the direction of Hijaz, and that was the reason for Salman’s migration to him and his belief in him.

The religion upon which the Muslims - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him - gathered in a clear and known meeting, is transmitted from their Prophet in frequent transmission. They narrated The Qur’an and they conveyed its Sunnah, and its Sunnah explains the Qur’an and clarifies it, as God Almighty said to it: {And We sent down to you the Remembrance that you may make clear to the people what It was revealed to them” [An-Nahl: 44].

So He explained the word and meaning of what God revealed, and it became the meanings of the Qur’an on which the Muslims clearly agreed, from what the nation inherited from Its Prophet, just as the words of the Qur’an were inherited from him, and there was - and praise be to God - what the nation agreed upon, there was nothing distorted and changed of meanings, so how? With words with those meanings.

Because its transmission and agreement on it is clearer than it in words, so it was the apparent religion of the Muslims that they agreed upon from what they transmitted from their Prophet. Its wording and meaning, and there was no distortion or alteration of either the word or the meaning, contrary to the Torah and the Gospel, for some of its words were changed. Its meanings and rulings, the Jews and Christians, or a combination of both, were an apparent change that was well-known among them, just as the Jews changed what was in the books. The foregoing of the good news of Christ and Muhammad, may God bless them and grant them peace, and the laws in the Torah and his command in some reports.
Just as the Christians changed much of the news, prophecies, and laws that Christ did not change, so what God abolished On the tongue of Christ from the Torah, Christ must be followed in it.

As for what was changed after Christ, such as the permissibility of pork meat and other things that God forbade but which Christ did not permit, and such as the abolition of circumcision Such as praying to the east (and increasing fasting and transferring it from time to time), taking pictures in churches, venerating the cross, and following Monasticism, for these are all laws that were not legislated by any of the prophets, not Christ, nor anyone else. They violated the law of God who was sent by them. the prophets, without God having legislated it on the tongue of a prophet.

The third aspect is that the Qur’an has been proven by necessarily known frequent transmission - for those who agree and disagree - that Muhammad - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him And peace be upon him - He used to say that it was the word of God, not his own, and that it was conveyed to him on behalf of God, and he used to differentiate between the Qur’an and what he spoke from the Sunnah, even if This was something that should be followed in faith and practice.

For God sent down to him the Book and wisdom, and taught his nation the Book and wisdom, as God Almighty said: “Indeed, God has conferred upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from among themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom. [Al Imran: 164].
And He Almighty said: {And remember the favor of God upon you and the Book and the wisdom He has sent down to you, advising you thereby} [Al-Baqarah: 231].
And God Almighty said: {And God has sent down to you the Book and wisdom and taught you what you did not know} [An-Nisa: 113].
And He Almighty said: {And remember what is recited in your homes of the signs of God and wisdom} [Al-Ahzab: 34].
And God Almighty said: On the authority of Hebron and his son Ishmael.

{Our Lord, make us submissive to You, and from our descendants a nation submissive to You, and show us our rituals, and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting, the Merciful} [Al-Baqarah: 128] (128) {Our Lord, and raise among them a messenger from among themselves who will recite to them Your verses, and teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them} [Al-Baqarah: 129].

The Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - said: “Indeed, I have been given the Book and something like it with it.” So he used to teach his nation the Book, which is the Mighty Qur’an which He told them that it was the word of God, not his own, about which He said: {Say, “If mankind and the jinn were gathered together to produce something like this... They will not produce the like of the Qur’an, even if they were [supporters] of one another.” [Al-Isra: 88].

And he is the one who legislated for his nation to recite it in their prayers, so no prayer is valid without it, and he taught them with that the wisdom that God sent down to him. He differentiated between it and the Qur’an in many ways.
Among them: that the Qur’an is miraculous.
Among them: The Qur’an is what is read in prayer without it.

Among them: The Arabic words of the Qur’an are revealed in the order of the verses, so no one has the right to change them in the Arabic language, according to the agreement of the Muslims. But it is permissible to interpret it in the Arabic language and translate it into a language other than Arabic.

As for reciting it in Arabic without its pronunciation, it is not permissible, according to Muslim agreement, contrary to what he taught them of wisdom, for it is not a ruling. Its wording is the same as the wording of the Qur’an, including: The Qur’an should not be touched by anyone except one who is pure, and should not be read by a person in a state of ritual impurity, as indicated by his Sunnah when he The masses of his nation, other than what is not the Qur’an.

The nation learned the Qur’an from him during his lifetime, and more than one of its companions memorized the entire Qur’an during his lifetime, and none of the companions memorized except those. He memorized some of it, and some of them memorized what others did not, so all of it was transmitted, heard from him, with frequent transmission, and he said that it Someone conveying it on behalf of God, and it is the word of God, not his.

There are many texts in the Qur’an - what makes it clear that it is the word of God - and those who saw Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and reported what they saw of His miracles, his deeds, his law, and what they heard from the Qur’an and his hadiths are thousands, consisting of more than a hundred thousand who saw and believed in him.

As for the Gospels that are in the hands of Christians: they are four Gospels: the Gospels of Matthew, John, Luke, and Mark, and they are agreed that Luke and Mark did not He sees Christ, but Matthew and John saw him, and these four articles which they call the Gospel, and they may call each one of them A Gospel. These people wrote it after Christ was taken up. They did not mention in it that it was the word of God, nor that Christ conveyed it on behalf of God. They transmitted some things from the words of Christ, and things from his deeds and miracles.

They mentioned that they did not narrate everything they heard and saw from him, as it was of the same type as what the people of hadith, biographies, and mystics narrate on the authority of the Prophet - May God bless him and grant him peace - from his words and actions that are not the Qur’an.
The Gospels in their hands resemble books of biography, books of hadith, or similar books, even if most of them are authentic.

Whatever he - peace be upon him - said, it was conveyed to him on the authority of God, in which it is necessary to believe his news and obey his command, as the Messenger said, and it is from the Sunnah. It is similar to what the Messenger said from the Sunnah, for among it is what the Messenger mentions as the saying of God as his saying.

God Almighty says: “Whoever is hostile to a friend of mine, I have declared war,” and similar to that, and among them is what he says, but it is also from what he revealed. God to him, so whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God, so this is what is conveyed in the Gospel, and it is of this type, for it was an order of Christ’s command is God’s command, and whoever obeys Christ has obeyed God.
Whatever Christ told about the unseen, God told him, for He is infallible to lie about what He tells.

If the Gospel resembles the revealed Sunnah, then there are errors in some of its words, as happens in the books of biography and the Sunan of Abu Dawud. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, then these books have become famous and widespread among Muslims (so no one can - after their fame and abundance Copies with it - to replace all of them.

But in some of its words there is an error that occurred before it became famous, so the hadith narrator - even if he is just - may make a mistake.) But what he received Muslims accept, believe, and act from the news, as it is what the majority of Muslims are certain is true from their Prophet.

This is the doctrine of the Salaf and the majority of the sects, such as the majority of the four sects and the majority of the theologians of the Kalabiyah and Karamiyya. And the Ash'arites and others, but some theologians thought that he could not be certain of its truthfulness because someone might make a mistake or lie. This suspicion is only directed towards a person whose truthfulness and accuracy are not known. However, if his truthfulness and accuracy are known, then it is through miracles. Like the prophets, either by the Prophet believing him in what he says, or by the infallible nation’s agreement on his truthfulness and their agreement to act on his information, or Their agreement to accept and acknowledge his news, and to mention him without objection, or the appearance of evidence, evidence, and clues that support his news, and the like. This is one of the indications of the truthfulness of the informer, so it is necessary to judge his truthfulness and that he did not lie or make mistakes, even if his information was If he were stripped of these evidences, it would be possible for him to be a lie or a mistake, just as a mere report does not confirm its lie unless there is evidence indicating that, either There is conclusive mental or auditory evidence that he is different from his informant, so he is certain that his information is false, and in that case the informant is either a liar. Or he is mistaken, and one of them may be known through evidence.

Muslims have information about their Prophet that is frequently transmitted and that which the infallible nation agreed to believe, and that it did not agree on. Evidence of his truthfulness from another direction, such as: if he told one, two, or three people in the presence of a large crowd, it is not permissible for him to They conspire to lie about news that they say those people have seen and witnessed, so they confirm this and none of them will deny it and know it. Due to the constant habit that if he were a liar, the consensus of the people of the Tawatir would not have prevented him from remaining silent about his denial, just as their agreement would not prevent him from deliberately Lying.

And if one and two narrated what custom requires to be made public and apparent, but it did not appear, and they narrated it concealing its narration, they did not narrate it directly. The heads of the public knew that they had lied about him.

The evidence for the truthfulness of the informer or his lie is many and varied, and this is not the place to list them, but what is meant here is that Muslims repeatedly They have on the authority of their Prophet the words of the Qur’an, its agreed-upon meanings, and the Mutawatir Sunnah, and they have much information on the authority of their Prophet. The knowledge of truthfulness in various ways, such as the truthfulness of an infallible nation, the evidence of customs, and so on, while they have memorized the Qur’an in their hearts, not In order to memorize it, they need an inscribed book. If the Qur’an was not available on the ground, that would not be a factor in what they had memorized.

Unlike the People of the Book, if there were no copies of the books, they would not have had a reliable transmission of their words, since he would not have preserved them - if He memorized it - except for a few whose memorization cannot be trusted. For this reason, after the cessation of prophecy from them, the People of the Book used to change the books. Either changing some of its provisions and meanings, or changing some of its words unless they correct it.

For this reason, there is no chain of transmission among them that the Muslims have, nor do they have any say in the transfer of knowledge, its amendment, its criticism, or knowledge of the conditions of its transfer. Knowledge does not belong to the Muslims, and there has been no auditory or rational evidence that they do not agree on a mistake. Rather, it is known that they agreed on a mistake. The mistake when they denied Christ.

Then they denied Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - since the books transmitted from the prophets were of the same type as the books transmitted from Muhammad and they did not It was frequently reported from them, and believing someone other than the infallible was not an argument. They did not have the knowledge to distinguish between truth and lies. Muslims.

These Gospels, which are in the hands of Christians of this kind, contain many of the words of Christ, his deeds, and his miracles, and they contain He made a mistake, without a doubt, and the one who wrote it in the first place, if he was not among those accused of intentionally lying, then the one, the two, and the three Of the four, it is not impossible for a mistake and forgetfulness to occur among them, especially what a person heard and saw and then narrated about it after many years. There are many mistakes in things like this, and there was no infallible nation whose reception of it with acceptance and belief would necessitate knowledge of it, lest The infallible nation gathers and the disciples are all twelve men.

The story of the crucifixion is one of the things that caused suspicion, as evidence has emerged that the crucified person was not Christ - peace be upon him - but rather an illusion resembling him. They thought he was the Messiah and the Apostles. None of them saw Christ crucified. Rather, some of the Jews who witnessed it told them of his crucifixion.

(Some people say: Indeed, those people deliberately lied, and most people say: They have been suspected, and for this reason the majority of Muslims used to say: His saying: {But it is made to appear to them} [An-Nisa’:

157] On the authority of those, and whoever says in the first place the pronoun in (it is similar to them) on the authority of those who heard the news of those, then if it is permissible for them to make a mistake in this, And they were not infallible in transmitting it. It is possible for them to make mistakes in some of what they transmit from it, and this is not something that discredits the message of Christ, nor in what... It has been repeatedly narrated from him that he is the Messenger of God who must be followed, whether he was crucified or not, and what has been narrated from him is that it is obligatory Believing in him, whether he was crucified or not.

The disciples are trustworthy in what they narrate from him. They are not accused of deliberately lying to him. But if some of them made mistakes in some of what they narrated, they would not This prevents it from being known to others, especially if the one he made a mistake in was one of the things his mistake in it has become clear in other places.

The Christians differed in general regarding what the error occurred, even in the crucifixion. Some of them say that the crucified person was not the Christ, but rather the likeness, as he says. Muslims, and among them are those who acknowledge their servitude to God and deny solutions and union, such as Arianism, and among them are those who deny union, even if he acknowledges With solutions like Nestorianism, and as for the laws that they follow, their scholars know that most of them are not about Christ - peace be upon him - so Christ He did not legislate for them the prayer to the east, nor the fifty days of fasting, nor doing it in the springtime, nor the feast of Christmas, the Epiphany, the feast of the cross, etc. That's who

Their festivals, and even more than that is what they invented after the Apostles, such as the Feast of the Cross, for it is what Helena of Harrania, the mother of Constantine, and in the time of Constantine, they changed a lot of the religion of Christ, its beliefs, and the laws, so they invented honesty, which is the doctrine of their faith. It is a belief that was not uttered in any of the books of the prophets that they have, nor was it transmitted from any of the prophets or from anyone else. Among the disciples who accompanied Christ, rather, a group of their elders invented it for them. They said they were three hundred and eighteen.

In doing so, they relied on similar words in the books, and in the books there are precise words that contradict what they mentioned, as has been explained elsewhere. And likewise are the general laws of their laws that they put in the Book of the Law, some of which were quoted from the prophets and some of which were quoted from the disciples. Many of what they invented were not transmitted from any of the prophets or from the disciples, although they were authorized by the greatest people of knowledge. And religion is to change the laws they saw and establish a new law. For this reason, most of their law was innovated, for which no book or law had been revealed. A prophet.

chapters.title: A chapter in response to their saying: How can our books, which are written in seventy-two tongues, be changed?
paragraphs: [Chapter: The response to their saying: How can our books be changed, which are written in seventy-two tongues?]

And as for their saying, “How is it possible to change our Books, which are written in seventy-two languages, and in each language of them such-and-such is a thousand copies of the Qur’an?” More than six hundred years passed until the advent of Muhammad?
It is said:

But after its widespread spread, the Muslims, and not even a well-known group of them, did not say that the words of every version in the world are It was changed, but the majority of Muslims who say that nothing has been changed in its words are only claiming that some of its words were changed before the message, or Changing some versions after the Resurrection does not change all the versions. Some people say that this change occurred at the beginning of the matter, and some of them say Some of them were changed after the sending of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and they do not say that every version in the world was changed, rather they say that some versions were changed Instead of some, and for many people, the altered versions appeared rather than the ones that were not altered.
The copies that have not been changed are still owned by some people.

It is known that this cannot be denied, as no one can know that every copy in the world in every language is identical to its wording. All copies in all tongues, except those who are aware of that, and they have accepted that no one is able to do that.

As for those who mentioned that the change occurred at the beginning, they say that the Gospels were taken from four people, two of whom were not seen. Christ. Rather, two of the Gospel writers, Matthew and John, saw him.
It is known that this can be changed.

As for their saying that it is written in seventy-two languages, it is known by Christian agreement that Christ only spoke in Hebrew. Like all the prophets of the children of Israel, and that he was circumcised, he was circumcised after the seventh, as the children of Israel are circumcised, and that he used to pray until He did not pray facing the east, nor was he commanded to pray facing the east.

Whoever says that his language was Syriac, as some people think, is mistaken, for the words that are transmitted about him in the Gospels are what he spoke. Hebrew and then translated from that language to another.

In translation, mistakes often occur, as we found in our time when someone translates the Torah from Hebrew to Arabic, and it appears in the translation from Error is what honest, intelligent people who know both languages attest to.
The Christians say that it was written in four languages: (Hebrew, Roman, Greek, and Syriac).

As for their saying that it was written in seventy-two languages, if this is true, it was written after those were written. The four, so if the mistake occurred in some of those four places, then writing it in seventy-two languages does not remove it. Muslims do not say: It was written in seventy-two languages, its pronunciation was changed in all tongues (for seventy-two languages in all A copy of that).

Rather, it is said that the change occurred before that, as is said in everything that was reported about Christ and Moses (and Muhammad - may God’s prayers and peace be upon them - from the hadith Such as the biography of Ibn Ishaq, the hadiths of the Sunan, and the chain of narrations on the authority of the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - for there is in the world every book of them. There are many copies, and it is not possible to change a long section of them, but in the same biography, mistakes occurred in places and hadiths that occurred in the Sunan, which are mistakes in The original (the fame of its copies after that does not prevent a mistake from occurring in the original) and these are the books of interpretation, jurisprudence, and details. A book that has many copies in the world, it is not possible to change a long section of it, and it contains hadiths that are wrong in the original.

The Gospels that are in the hands of the Christians are similar to this, and for this reason they were commanded to judge according to what they contain, for in them are the rulings of God and in general what they contain. The wording of the rulings was not changed, but rather some of the words of the information and some of the meanings of the matters were changed, as we are commanded to do with hadiths. The rulings known from the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - the scholars paid more attention to controlling them than they did to controlling them. Information such as hadiths of asceticism, stories, virtues, and the like, since the need of nations to know commands and prohibitions is greater than Their need to know the details of the information that general faith is sufficient for.

As for commands and prohibitions, it is necessary to know them in detail, because following what is commanded can only be detailed, and what is prohibited is obligatory. Avoiding it must distinguish between it and other things, as God Almighty said: {And God would never mislead a people after He had guided them until He had made clear to them What they fear.” [At-Tawbah: 115].

Christians do not need this for themselves, as it is not obligatory for them to adhere to a law transmitted from Christ - upon him. Peace be upon them - and among them it is permissible for their elders to legislate a religion that Christ did not legislate, and they say: What these people legislated was legislated by Christ and it was not They have care and no knowledge of the law of Christ, just as Muslims have care and knowledge of the law of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace.

chapters.title: A chapter responding to their saying that the Torah was taken from Al-Uzair and he was an infallible prophet
paragraphs: [Chapter: The response to their saying that the Torah was taken from Al-Uzayr and he was an infallible prophet]

As for the Torah, it is known among Muslims, Jews, and Christians that the Holy House was destroyed the first time, and its people were evacuated from it. They were taken captive, and there were not many apparent copies of the Torah. Rather, it was taken from a small group.

They also say that Uzair dictated it, and that they found another copy, so they corresponded with it, and the correspondence takes place with two people, and one of them may make a mistake. They mention that among the kings there were those who ordered seventy-two of their rabbis to copy them, and he considered some of those copies with others, and this is so. It was true, which does not prevent the fact that a mistake occurred in some of its words before that, unless it is proven that they were taken from an infallible prophet or All its words were approved by an infallible Prophet.
What the infallible one said is the truth, and what is proven by mutawatir transmission is the truth.
And those who say that some of its words were changed at that time say that it was not taken from an infallible prophet, nor was it transmitted with frequent transmission.

Whoever disputes from among the Muslims and the People of the Book say: It was taken from Al-Uzair, and he is an infallible prophet, and this is what needs to be proven. And the one who does not want to achieve it.

And if the Christians say that Christ - peace be upon him - approved it, it is said that Christ - peace be upon him - could not oblige them to do what God has obligated upon them. Of faith in him and obedience to him, how could he have changed the copies of the Torah that they had, even though there were many of them, even though they had asked for him to be killed? And they crucified him because of his incapacity and weakness, and they crucified his likeness as the Muslims say, or they crucified him himself (as the Christians say), so how could he Should he fix what was changed?

As for those after Christ, he is not infallible, and Christ changed some of its rulings and approved most of them, and the rulings are only claimed by Muslims. Abrogating and changing it by believing contrary to its reason and acting accordingly, they do not need a claim to change its words, just as they changed the law Stoning for anything other than that is written in the Torah.
Contrary to the reports, most Muslims say that the change occurred in some of its words.

As for the prophecies transmitted from the twenty-two prophets, not a single prophecy of which all of its words are repeated is known. Its best condition is for it to be like the Gospel, and it is like what is transmitted from the sayings of the prophets and their lives, such as the story of Ibn Ishaq or some of the books of Musnads and Sunan in which what the transmitters transmit of the sayings of the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - and his actions are transmitted. Most of it is true, and some of it is false.
But for this nation, God preserved what He sent down, as God Almighty said: {Indeed, it is We who have sent down the Remembrance, and indeed, We will preserve it} [Al-Hijr: 9].

So whatever error is in the interpretation of the Qur’an, or the transmission of the Hadith, or its interpretation, God will raise up for it from among the nation someone who will clarify it and mention the evidence for it. The mistake of the blunderer and the lies of the liar, for this nation will not unite upon misguidance, and there will continue to be a group within it that is victorious on the truth until it rises. The Hour when they will be the last of the nations, and there will be no prophet - after their prophet - after them, and no book after their book.

And when the nations before them changed and changed, God sent a prophet to explain to them, command them, and forbid them, and there was no longer Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace. May God bless him and grant him peace - a prophet, and God has guaranteed that he will preserve what He sent down of the message, and that this nation will not unite upon misguidance, but rather God has raised up for this nation in every age those from among the people of knowledge and the Qur’an who will preserve their religion through it and ward off the distortion and plagiarism of the extremists. Misguided people and the interpretation of the ignorant.

chapters.title: A chapter on responding to those who said that he changed some of its words after sending Muhammad
paragraphs: [Chapter: The response to those who said that some of its words were changed after the sending of Muhammad]

As for those who say: He changed some of its words after sending Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - these people say: It was in the Torah. The Gospel and other than them are clear words that state matters.
Among them is the name of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and that he baptized some of the People of the Book, so they changed some of the words in the copies that they had.

They do not say: These people changed every version that was on the face of the earth, but they changed some of the words of the versions, and the people wrote from those versions. Many versions were changed and spread, so that most of what is found among many of the People of the Book is from those changed versions.

There are other copies in the world that have not been changed, so many people mentioned that they saw and read them, and in those copies there is something that is not in the other copies, and what indicates that This is because in this time, if you took the copies of the Torah available to the Jews, Christians, and Samaria, you would find a difference between them in Multiple locations.

Likewise, the copies of the Gospel, and likewise the copies of the Psalms, differ greatly to the point that the rational person does not believe that all existing copies of the Torah They agree on one word, and it is not known that all versions of the Gospel agree on one word, and it is not known that all versions of the Psalms agree on one word. One, in addition to all the other prophecies.

It is known that the People of the Book cannot establish an argument that all versions in all languages in all corners of the earth agree on one word. In all that exists, of all prophecies, and the argument they used as evidence of the impossibility of changing them, all indicate the impossibility of knowledge. All of them are equal.

So when they say: Who is it that speaks with seventy-two tongues, and who is it that judges over the entire world, its kings and its priests? And its scholars until He judged everyone by the diameters of the earth and gathered them from the four corners of the earth (until He changed them.

It was said to them: Who is he who knows seventy-two languages? And who is he who ruled over the world, its kings, its priests, and its scholars, until he judged And he gathered every copy that existed throughout the earth and met every copy. (It exists in all the earth) in all versions, and he found all the words in all the versions that have seventy-two tongues from all the corners of the earth as words. Agreed, he did not change her words.

The claim of knowledge of this is more impossible than the claim of changing it, for if anyone were able to collect all the copies, it would be His ability to change all of its words is easier for him than it is to replace everything in one copy with everything in the other copies.

If we brought ten copies of a book, changing some of the ten words would be easier for us than changing every one of the ten. With the remaining nine, since the interview requires knowing all the words of each version and their equality with the other.

As for change, it is sufficient for him to change from each copy what he would change from the other, even if changing all copies is usually unavoidable. Knowing that they are in agreement is more impossible, and if knowledge of their agreement is possible, then the possibility of changing some of their words is easier and easier.
As for their statement, if it is said that he changed some of it and left out some of it, this cannot be because it is all one statement and wording. One in all tongues.

It is said: The possibility of saying this is apparent and cannot be disputed by a rational person, and it is a reality, for we have seen the Torah that Samaria has in contradiction with The Torah of the Jews and Christians (even in the ten words.

So Samaria mentioned therein the matter of facing the Mount something that is not found in the Jewish and Christian versions. Likewise, there is a difference between the Jewish and Christian versions. It is well known that the versions of the Gospel are different, and the versions of the Psalms are different even more than that. In any case, no rational person can say: Some copies may not be changed.
But if they say that none of it has been changed because it is all one statement and one expression in all tongues, then this claim is invalid. Two faces.

One of them: that knowledge’s claim that all copies are equal is more eloquent than the claim of the possibility of changing them. If change is impossible for all of them, then One person’s knowledge of what is in all of them - and that their words are similar despite the differences in tongues - is more deserving of abstinence.

Second: This is a claim that is contrary to reality, as the difference in the versions of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms exists and we have seen it with our own eyes. And others saw it, so I saw several versions of the Psalms that differ greatly from one another, and we saw some of the words of the Torah that this one conveys. The sect, while it is written by them, they claim that it is the correct Torah transmitted by them with frequent transmission, contradicts some of the words of the Torah. The other sect, as well as the Gospel.

In short, they say: This cannot be; Because it is all one saying and one expression in all tongues, it included two things: it included a false claim, and a false argument. Their saying: (This is not possible) is apparent arrogance, as the possibility of changing some versions is something no rational person would dispute about its possibility, but he might say Who said:

If some of the versions were changed and that was revealed, then that became widespread and the rest of the people of the versions saw that version as different from their versions and they denied it. There are motives and motives to deny this, just as there is such a thing today if a man wanted to change a book that is well known to people, with it. Multiple copies, so if he changes it and that copy reaches someone who knows what is in those copies, they deny that.

It is said: This is possible if that changed version reaches a group that is forbidden from conspiring with them in lying, for it is as In repeated reports, it is impossible to conspire to lie, so it is impossible to conspire to conceal what is usually impossible to conceal.

It is known that it is not forbidden for a small group to conspire to change some copies, and the copies only exist with scholars. The People of the Book, not their common people, memorizes its words as the common Muslims memorize the words of the Qur’an. So if a group of them intended to change A copy or copies they have, that is possible, then if another sect colluded not to mention that, that is possible, but if The sects were among those who could not conspire to lie or conceal, so this was impossible among them.

We have seen among the People of the Book books that they claim to have from the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - in the handwriting of Ali bin Abi Talib, in which there are matters It relates to their purposes, and many Muslims were confused about it, and they glorified what was in it and gave the People of the Book what was written for them in it. Believing that they were following what was in it, then when it reached whomever of the Muslim scholars it had reached, they demonstrated its falsity in known ways. Repeatedly, such as their mention therein: Ka’b ibn Malik al-Ahbar bore witness to the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - meaning Ka’b ibn Malik al-Ahbar.

Ka’b al-Ahbar only converted to Islam during the reign of Omar ibn al-Khattab, when the Prophet did not reach him. His name was Ka’b ibn Mati’, but among the Ansar was Ka’b ibn Malik is the poet whose repentance God revealed in Surah (Baraa), so these ignorant people thought that this was that.

An example of their mention of the martyrdom of Saad bin Muadh, whose death shook the throne of the Most Gracious, they mentioned his martyrdom in the year of Khaybar, and the people of Knowing that he died after the Battle of the Trench, some time before the Battle of Khaybar, and the like.

As for their refuting argument, they say: All the books of prophecies that are in the world, including the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the prophecies, exist. With seventy-two tongues, with one expression and one statement. Can any of the wise people say that he knew that?

And he knew that every version of the twenty-four prophecies in one of the seventy-two tongues agrees with every version in all other languages. Tongues, even if someone claimed that every copy of the Torah in the world is in the Arabic language (or every copy of the Bible in the world is in the Arabic language) Arabic) or every copy in the world of the Psalms in the Arabic language that agrees with all the Arabic copies that exist in the corners of the world. He claimed what he did not know and could not know, so where did he get that from?
Has he seen every Arabic version of these books, or has someone who knows his honesty told him that all the Arabic versions in the world Is this version compatible?
Likewise, if he claimed that in the Greek, Syriac, and Roman languages,

And the Hebrew, and the Indian, and if there are in the world in every book of these seventy-two languages, then the claim of agreement to abrogate every language of its kind The claim of agreement in Arabic versions. So what if he claimed agreement in Arabic versions in all languages?
Assuming that this could be said in versions of a language transmitted by its people and its speakers, how can its claim be made in a language with so many speakers? And its people spread out?

This is not like the claim that the Mus-hafs of Muslims agree with the Qur’an, as the transmission of the Qur’an does not depend on the Qur’an, rather the Qur’an is preserved in the hearts of people. Thousands and thousands of Muslims, whose number can only be counted by God Almighty. If every Qur’an in the world did not exist, this would not constitute a reason for quoting a word from The words of the Qur’an, in contrast to the previous books. It is rare for us to find anyone among the People of the Book who has memorized any of these books. There are some Jews who memorize the Torah.

As for the Christians, there is no one among them who has memorized the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the prophecies as a whole, let alone memorizing them with two And seventy tongues, (and if that is found, it is a small number, and neither lies nor error are prevented from them.)

So it became clear that what they mentioned about the spread of their books in different tongues is one of the strongest matters regarding the lack of knowledge of the similarity of what is in them. Of words, and if the Qur’an is transmitted in one language, and that language is preserved by many Muslims, then that is Which shows that no one can change any of its words in the Qur’an, even if it is possible to change some words in the Torah and the Gospel when Many of the People of the Book.

Muslims do not claim that he changed all the words of all the copies after sending the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - as these people thought of them. The ignorant people, rather, they claimed what is justified by reason, and evidence of its truth appears, but these ignorant people claimed knowledge, that all copies In all tongues, in all scriptures, with one word, so claim what no one can know, and claim what is known to be false.

chapters.title: Chapter on proving differences and changes in the versions of the People of the Book
paragraphs: [Chapter: Proving disagreement and change in the versions of the People of the Book]

The answer appeared from their saying: Who is it that speaks with seventy-two tongues, or who is it that rules over the entire world? its kings, its priests, and its scholars until he ruled over the entire world from the four corners of the world until he changed it, even if that was what he was able to do. Collect all or some of them.
This is not possible, since they are all one saying, one text, and one belief.

The answer to that has appeared in several ways: One of them is: We did not claim to change it after it came out on these tongues and became widespread. Copies. Rather, we do not claim change after the spread of copies in what is not from the books of the Prophets, such as books of grammar, medicine, arithmetic, hadiths, and Sunnahs. What was transmitted from the Prophets was originally transmitted by a single person, then many copies of it became widespread. No one claims that it is after The spread of copies of a book in the east and west of the earth. A man ruled over the entire world, and he collected the copies that were in it and changed them.
No one claimed like that in the Torah and the Gospel, but he only claimed that in them, since the copies were few: either a copy, or Two, or four, and so on.
Or he claimed to have changed some of the words of the copies, because some copies can be changed.
There are copies of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms that exist today, and there is some disagreement, but it is a small difference, and most of them are in agreement.
This is evident from the second aspect: that their saying: It is all one saying, one text, and one belief, is not what they said, but rather abrogated. The Torah is different in places.

There is a difference between the Torah of the Jews, Christians, and Samaria, and between the copies of the Psalms there is more difference than that, and likewise between the Gospels, so how were the copies Prophecies?

I have seen some of the copies of the Psalms that contain a declaration of the prophecy of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - in his name, and I saw another copy of the Psalms, but I did not see That is in it, and at that time it is not impossible for some versions of the attributes of the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - to be present in others.

The third aspect: The change in interpretation is a matter about which there is no doubt, and through it the purpose is achieved in this situation, for we know for sure that he mentioned Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - was written in what existed in his time of the Torah and the Gospel, as God Almighty said: {Which they find written With them in the Torah and the Gospel} [Al-A’raf: 157].
There is no doubt that the copies of the Torah and the Gospel during his reign were numerous and spread throughout the east and west of the earth, so there must be one of two things.
Either the wording was changed in some versions and the changed versions spread.

Or it was mentioned in all versions, as many scholars have extracted it from among the rabbis of the Jews and Christians and those who were not. From their rabbis, they extracted mention of him and the good news of him in many different places in the Torah, the Gospel, and the prophecies of the prophets. As it is explained elsewhere.
And whoever says that his mention is found in it more than this, and he explicitly states it in some versions, these people cannot refute him by saying:

We have looked at every version in the world of the Torah and the Gospel in the east and west of the earth, and we found it to be on the same wording. This is said by no one but a liar, for it is not possible for a human being to look at every copy in the east and west of the earth, just as it is not possible for him To change every version in the east and west of the earth. If he did not know the differences in the versions, he could not be certain of their agreement in wording. So how? Have people familiar with it mentioned the difference in its pronunciation?
What shows that the one who claimed that its pronunciation is identical is a lie (and how can its pronunciation be identical when it is in different languages)?

chapters.title: Chapter refuting the Christians’ claim that the Qur’an approved them as they were
paragraphs: [Chapter: Refuting the Christians’ claim that the Qur’an approved of them as they are upon]

They said: Then we found in this book, what is greater proof than this, such as his saying in Surat Al-Shura: {And say, “I believe in what God has revealed.” From the Book, and I have been commanded to be just between you. God is our Lord and your Lord. We have our works and you have your works. There is no argument between us and you. God will bring us together and to Him. Destiny} [Al-Shura: 15].

And as for those other than the People of the Book, He says: {Say, O disbelievers} [Al-Kafirun: 1] (1) {I do not worship what you worship} [Al-Kafirun: 2] (2) {Nor are you worshipers. What I worship} [Al-Kafirun: 3]. . . The entire surah. The answer: As for his saying: {And say, “I believe in the Book that God has sent down, and I have been commanded to do justice between you. God is our Lord and your Lord. We have our works and you have them.” Your deeds are no argument between us and you} [Al-Shura: 15].

This verse is mentioned after His - the Most High - saying: {He has prescribed for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and what We have revealed to you and what We have enjoined upon it. Abraham, Moses, and Jesus: Establish the religion and do not become divided in it. Hard for the polytheists is what you call them to. God chooses to Him whom He wills and guides. To Him is he who turns.} [Al-Shura: 13] (13) {And they did not disperse except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves, and had it not been for a word that had preceded from your Lord for a term. It was decided between them, and those to whom the Book was inherited after them are in doubt about it, doubtful.} [Al-Shura:

14] (14) {Therefore pray and be steadfast as you have been commanded, and do not follow their desires, and say, “I believe in what God has sent down of the Book, and I have been commanded, that God may be just among you.” Our Lord and your Lord} [Al-Shura: 15].

He has told us that He has legislated for us the religion that which He commanded Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus: “Establish the religion, and do not become divided concerning it,” as God Almighty said. In the other verse: {So set your face upright toward religion, the nature of God which He has created mankind upon. There is no altering of God’s creation. That is the noble religion, but Most people do not know} [Al-Rum: 30] (30) {Turn to Him, and fear Him, and establish prayer, and do not be of the polytheists} [Al-Rum: 31] (31) {Of those who were divided. their religion and they were sects, each party rejoicing in what they had” [Al-Rum: 32].

And He Almighty said: {O Messengers, eat of the good things and do righteousness. Indeed, I am All-Knowing of what you do.} [Al-Mu’minun: 51] (51) {And this is your nation, a nation. One, and I am your Lord, so fear Me} [Al-Mu’minun: 52] (52) {Then they divided their affairs among themselves into sects, every party rejoicing in what they have.} [Al-Mu’minun: 53].

Then he told about the division of those who were given the Book, like the division of the Jews and Christians, and the division of the Jewish groups, and the Christian groups, like the Nestorians. Jacobism and the monarchy.
Then He said: {And those who were given the Book after them in inheritance} [Al-Shura: 14] - those are the divided ones - {there is doubt about it, one who doubts} [Al-Shura: 14].
Thus, the generality of Jews and Christians is in doubt about this.

And He - the Most High - said: {And We gave Moses the Scripture, but they differed therein. And had it not been for a word that had preceded from your Lord, it would have been decided between them, and indeed they are in doubt concerning it. suspicious} [Fussilat: 45].

And God Almighty said: {And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear to them. And indeed, those who differ concerning it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except They followed suspicion, and they did not kill him with certainty} [An-Nisa: 157] (157) {Rather, God raised him to Himself, and God is Mighty, All-Wise} [An-Nisa: 158].
Then He - the Almighty - said: {Therefore, call upon and be upright as you have been commanded} [Al-Shura: 15].
To the religion that He has legislated for us: {And be steadfast as you have been commanded, and do not follow their desires} [Al-Shura: 15].

This deals with the desires of the People of the Book, just as it deals with the desires of the polytheists, and He made that clear in His saying - the Most High -: {And you will never be satisfied. From the Jews or the Christians until you follow their religion. Say, “Indeed, the guidance of God is the right guidance,” even if you follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you. You have in God neither guardian nor helper” [Al-Baqarah: 120].

And He Almighty said: {And if you brought to those who were given the Book every sign, they would not follow your qiblah, nor will you follow their qiblah, nor will some of them follow. The direction of another, and if you were to follow their desires, after the knowledge that has come to you, then you would certainly be among the wrongdoers.} [Al-Baqarah: 145].

He also stated His prohibition against following the desires of the polytheists in His saying - the Most High -: {Say: Bring forth your witnesses who bear witness that God has forbidden this. But if they bear witness, do not bear witness with them, and do not follow the inclinations of those who deny Our signs, and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, but they are just to their Lord.} [Al-An'am: 150]
And He - the Almighty - said: {And say, “I believe in what God has sent down of the Book” [Al-Shura: 15].

Indeed, God has commanded him and all of creation to believe in everything that God has revealed, and likewise His saying - the Most High -: {And I have been commanded to be just among you} [Al-Shura: 15].
For God commanded him to be just among all of creation, and He said: “Allah is our Lord and your Lord. We have our works and you have your works” [Al-Shura: 15].

This is his disavowal of the polytheists and the People of the Book whom he addresses with this, as God Almighty says: {And if they deny you, then tell me my work and yours. You are innocent of what I do, and I am innocent of what you do” [Yunus: 41].

An example of it is His saying - the Almighty -: {Say, “Do you dispute with us about God, when He is our Lord and your Lord, and We have our works and you have your works, and we are sincere to Him} [Al-Baqarah: 139].

And likewise His saying: {Say, O disbelievers} [Al-Kafirun: 1] (1) {I do not worship what you worship} [Al-Kafirun: 2] (2) {And you are not worshipers of what I worship} [Al-Kafirun: 3] (3) {Nor am I a worshiper of what you worshiped} [Al-Kafirun: 4] (4) {Nor are you worshipers of what I worship} [Al-Kafirun: 5] (5) {You have your religion and I have my religion} [Al-Kafirun: 6].
This word is like His saying: “I have my work and you have your work. You are innocent of what I do and I am innocent of what you do” [Yunus: 41].

It is a word that necessitates his innocence from their work and their innocence from his work, as the letter Lām in the Arabic language indicates specialization, so his saying: {For you. Your religion is my religion” [Al-Kafirun: 6].

It indicates that you are specific to your religion and I do not share it with you, and I am specific to my religion and you do not share it with me, as He said: {I have my work and you have your work. You are innocent of what I do and I am innocent of what you do” [Yunus: 41].

For this reason, “the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - said in {Say, O disbelievers} [Al-Kafirun: 1] It is an acquittal from polytheism,” and it is not in this verse that He was satisfied with the religion of the polytheists or the People of the Book, as some atheists think, nor did He forbid their jihad, as some misguided people thought. And they made it abrogated, but rather it contains his disavowal of their religion and their disavowal of his religion, and that their deeds will not harm him nor will they be rewarded for his work nor will It benefits them.

This is a decisive matter that cannot be abrogated. The Messenger was not satisfied with the religion of the polytheists, nor were the People of the Book for the blink of an eye. And whoever claims that he was satisfied The religion of the disbelievers, and he used as evidence His saying - the Most High -: {Say, O disbelievers} [Al-Kafirun: 1] (1) {I do not worship what you worship} [Al-Kafirun: 2] (2) {And neither do you. You worship what I worship. And I have a religion} [Al-Kafirun: 6].

(So this atheist thought that his saying: {You have your religion and I have my religion} [Al-Kafirun: 6] meant that he was satisfied with the religion of the disbelievers. Then he said: This verse abrogated, so he has accepted the religion of the disbelievers), and this is among the clearest lies and slander against Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace -, for he did not He was never satisfied except with the religion of God with which He sent His messengers, and with which He sent down His books. He was never satisfied with the religion of the disbelievers, neither of the polytheists nor of their people. The book.

And his saying: {You have your religion and I have mine} [Al-Kafirun: 6] does not indicate his satisfaction with their religion, nor their approval of it, rather it indicates his innocence of Their religion, and for this reason the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - said (Indeed, this Surah is a disavowal of polytheism).

The equivalent of this verse is His saying - the Most High -: {And if they deny you, then tell me my work and you have your work. You are innocent of what I do and I am innocent of what you do} [Yunus: 41].

Likewise, God Almighty says: “Therefore, call upon and be steadfast as you have been commanded, and do not follow their desires, and say, ‘I believe in what God has sent down of the Book.’” And I have been commanded to do justice between you. God is our Lord and your Lord. We have our deeds and you have your deeds” [Al-Shura: 15].

Some people may also think that his saying {You have your religion and I have mine} [Al-Kafirun: 6] the verse, that I do not command fighting, nor forbid it, nor I deny it and do not confirm it. Rather, it is that your religion is yours and you are specific to it and I am free from it, and my religion is mine and I am specific to it. And you are innocent of it.
This is a decisive matter that cannot be abrogated under any circumstances, as God Almighty said on the authority of Al-Khalil.

{And when Abraham said to his father and his people, “Indeed, I am disavowed from what you worship} [Al-Zukhruf: 26] (26) {Except Him who created me. Indeed, it is He who will guide us} [Al-Zukhruf: 27].
And God Almighty said: {And every human being We have bound his bird around his neck} [Al-Isra: 13].

And it is what has escaped him of good and evil, and He - the Most High - said: {And every soul does not earn except for its own sake, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another.} [Al-An’am: 164] .
And God Almighty said: “To her is what she earned, and upon her is what she earned.” [Al-Baqarah: 286]

And He - the Almighty - said: {If you do good, you will do good to yourselves, and if you do evil, then it will be yours.} [Al-Isra: 7]. Rather, He - the Most High - said to His Prophet: {And lower Your wing is for those of the believers who follow you.} [Al-Shu’ara’: 215] (215) {Then if they disobey you, say, “Indeed, I am disavowed of what you do.” [Al-Shu’ara’: 216].

If God had absolved him of the disobedience of those of His faithful followers who disobeyed him, then how could He not acquit him of the disbelief of the unbelievers, who are more severe? Is he disobedient or disobedient? !

chapters.title: Chapter on the obligation of Jews and Christians to follow the religion of Islam
paragraphs: [Chapter: Obligating Jews and Christians to follow the religion of Islam]

As for His saying - the Almighty -: {Say, O disbelievers} [Al-Kafirun: 1] (1) {I do not worship what you worship} [Al-Kafirun: 2] (2) {Nor do you worship what I worship} [Al-Kafirun: 3] (3) {Nor am I a worshiper of what you worshipped} [Al-Kafirun: 4] (4) {Nor are you worshipers of what I worship} [Al-Kafirun: 5] (5) {You have your religion and I have a religion} [Al-Kafirun: 6] It is a command to say to all the unbelievers, whether the polytheists or the People of the Book, for the People of the Book who do not believe in what was revealed to them His Lord is disbelievers. He has testified against them of disbelief and commanded their jihad. He has declared disbelief to those whom He has not made disbelievers and made it obligatory for them to be jihad. God Almighty said:
{The disbelievers from among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not to dissipate until clear proof came to them} [Al-Baynah: 1].
And He - the Almighty - said: {Indeed, those who say that God is the Messiah, the son of Mary, have disbelieved} [Al-Maeda: 17].
And He - the Almighty - said: {Indeed, those who say that God is the third of three have disbelieved} [Al-Maeda: 73].

And God Almighty said: {Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, and do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not follow the religion of truth. Those who were given the Book until they were given the tribute with help, but they were humble.} [At-Tawbah: 29].

The letter (from) in these places indicates gender, so it shows the gender of the preceding word, even if what came before it includes all the genders that After that, other than when it was for simplification, such as his saying: {Those who disbelieved are not among the People of the Book} [Al-Bayyinah: 1].
For among those who disbelieved after the sending of the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - are included all the polytheists and the People of the Book.

Likewise, those who do not believe in God or the Last Day, and do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not follow the religion of truth, are all people of The Book to whom His call reached them, but they did not believe in it, and likewise His saying: {Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds} [An-Nour: 55].

And if all of them were those who believed and did righteous deeds, and this is if the type includes the mentioned and others, but nothing remains in the type except Those mentioned, as he says: Here is a man from Banu Abdul Muttalib, even if there is no one else left of them.

He described them as polytheists, and that they worship other than God, as God Almighty said: {They took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God. And the Messiah is the son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God. There is no god but Him. Glory be to Him above what they associate with Him.} [At-Tawbah: 31].

So he informed that they had taken lords other than God, and they had taken Christ as their Lord, and they were commanded only to worship one God, and these people, by taking Other lords whom they worshiped, so they associated others with God - Glory be to Him, Most High above what they associate with Him.

And He Almighty said: {It is not for a human being that God should give him the Book and judgment and prophecy and then say to the people, “Be my servants instead of God.” But Be rabbinic in that you teach the Scripture and in that in which you study.} [Al Imran: 79] (79) And He does not command you to take the angels. And the prophets are lords. Who can command you to disbelief after you have submitted?} [Al Imran: 80].
He also told that whoever takes the angels and the prophets as lords is an unbeliever.

And He Almighty said: {Those who say that God is the third of three have certainly disbelieved, and there is no god but one god, and if they do not desist from what they say, they will certainly touch. Those who disbelieve among them will receive a painful punishment} [Al-Maeda: 73] (73) {Will they not repent to God and seek His forgiveness, and God is Forgiving and Merciful} [Al-Maeda: 74] (74) {What The Messiah, the son of Mary, except a messenger. The messengers had passed away before him, and his mother was a truthful one. They used to eat food. See how We make clear to them the signs. Then See how they are misled.} [Al-Ma’idah:
75] (75) {Say, “Do you worship besides God that which can do you no harm or benefit? And God is the Hearer, the Knower.” [Al-Ma’idah: 76]

(He rebuked the people of the Trinity because they worship that which can do them neither harm nor benefit. And God is the Hearer, the Knower.) So they included in his saying: {Say, O disbelievers} [Al-Kafirun: 1] (1) {I do not worship what you worship} [Al-Kafirun: 2] (2) {Nor are you worshipers of what I worship} [Al-Kafirun: 3].

Other disbelievers have also entered into this, especially since the Jews have entered into this, and they are more deserving of entering than others, for his saying: (What You worship) deals with the attributes of the object of worship, and the God whom the believers worship is the God who sent down the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur’an. And He sent Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad - may God’s prayers and peace be upon them.

The God who is characterized by these qualities is not worshiped by Jews and Christians, and this is like His saying: {They said, “We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham.” Ishmael and Isaac are one God, and to Him we submit.” [Al-Baqarah: 133].

This is the God that Muhammad and his nation worship, and he is not the God of the polytheists that they worship, even though He is the One who deserves to be They worship Him, for they associate partners with His worship, and describe Him with something of which He is free, so they are not sincere in religion to Him, so they worship other gods with Him, if not They are too arrogant to worship Him, and the God of the servant whom He actually worships is not the same with Him as He is with the One who deserves to be worshiped, and He is He does not worship Him, but rather associates anything with Him or is too arrogant to worship Him. This is what He said about it: {I do not worship what you worship} [Al-Kafirun: 2].
Polytheism prevails among Christians, and arrogance prevails among Jews.

chapters.title: Chapter on the obligation of arguing with the oppressors, whether polytheists or People of the Book
paragraphs: [Chapter: The obligation of debating with the wrongdoers, whether polytheists or the People of the Book]
As for his saying: {There is no argument between us and you} [Al-Shura: 15].

The verse, this is not a speech to Christians in particular, but rather it is a speech to everyone, and these Christians thought that the meaning of this was: Do not argue with the people of The Book, as they thought in the Almighty’s saying: “And do not dispute with the People of the Book except in a way that is best, except those who are unjust among them” [Al-Ankabut: 46].
What it means is: Do not argue with the People of the Book - that is, the Christians - except in a way that is best, except with those who are unjust, that is, the Jews.

This is a distortion of the Word of God from its context, and it is similar to their distortion of what they have of the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and all the rest. The prophecies, for they are greater in power over distorting their meanings than they are over distorting the meanings of the Qur’an, since the Qur’an had a nation that memorized it. You know its meanings, and you ward off anyone who distorts its wording or meaning.
As for those books, they do not have anyone who can distort their wording and meaning. That is why their distortion of them was great, and it was greater than their distortion. For the Qur’an.

What makes it clear that this speech is not specific to Christians is that this surah is Meccan, and the Meccan surahs were addressed to those who do not read. The Book, it is not specific to the People of the Book, but rather it applies to nations or is specific to the polytheists.

The Medinan surahs sometimes address the People of the Book, sometimes they are specific to the believers, and sometimes they are general. And God Almighty said: The polytheists are whatever you call them to. Allah chooses to Him whom He wills and guides to Him whomever turns.” [Al-Shura: 13].

And He, the Most High, said: {And they did not separate except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves. And had it not been for a word that had preceded from your Lord, for an appointed time, it would have been decreed. among them, and indeed those who were bequeathed to them the Book after them are in doubt about it, doubting it.} [Al-Shura: 14].

The speech either includes the polytheists and the People of the Book, or it concerns the polytheists and the People of the Book: the Jews, the Christians, and all An estimate, so there is no basis for singling it out to Christians.
As for His saying - the Most High -: {There is no argument between us and you} [Al-Shura: 15].

It is similar to the Almighty’s saying: {Say, “Do you dispute with us about God, when He is our Lord and your Lord, and We have our works and you have your works, and we are sincere to Him} [Al-Baqarah: 139].
