And He said: {And if they dispute with you, then say, “I have submitted my face to God and to those who follow me, and say to those who were given the Scripture and the unlettered people, ‘Have you submitted?’” If they submit, Indeed, they are guided, and if they turn away, it is your responsibility only to convey the message} [Al Imran: 20].
Hujjah is a name for what is used as evidence, whether right or wrong, as he said.
{So that the people may have no argument against you, except those among them who are wrong} [Al-Baqarah: 150].
The wrongdoers are protesting against you with a false argument, like the polytheists saying: When the qiblah was turned to the Kaaba, it returned to your qiblah. He will return to your religion,
This is a refuting argument from the oppressors.

And what makes this clear is his saying after that: {And those who dispute about God after He has been answered, their argument is disproven before their Lord. And upon them is wrath, and for them is a severe punishment} [Al-Shura: 16].
So he called it proof and made it refuting, and those who argue about God after He has been answered are the disbelievers from among the polytheists and the People of the Book.

They dispute with the believers to turn them away from their religion, and he said about the Christians: {So whoever disputes with you about it after the knowledge that has come to you, say, Come. We will call upon our sons and your sons, and our women and your women, and our selves and your selves, and then let us pray and bestow the curse of God upon the liars.} [Al Imran: 61] .

The unbelievers used to argue with the believers until they turned them away from their religion, just as they were harming them. Their argument was refuted by their Lord, and it was against them. Anger, and for them is a severe torment.

And their argument with the believers is out of injustice towards them, aggression against them, and falsehood. So He, the Most High, commanded him to say: {There is no argument between us. And among you} [Al-Shura: 15].
That is, you do not have the right to oppress us or attack us with your refuting arguments.
This does not mean that we do not debate with you and call you to the truth with sound arguments.
For God Almighty said: “Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best” [An-Nahl: 125].
So God Almighty commanded him to debate with the people of his calling, absolutely from the polytheists, and from the People of the Book in a way that is best.
And God Almighty said: {And do not dispute with the People of the Book except in a way that is best, except with those who are unjust among them} [Al-Ankabut: 46].

The wrongdoer is a transgressor and deserves punishment, so it is permissible for him to be punished with the punishment he deserves. It should not be limited to what it is. Better, unlike the one who did not do wrong, for he only argues in a way that is best.

People of the Book is a name that refers to the Jews and Christians, as in its counterparts in the Qur’an, such as His - the Most High - saying: {And the food of those who were given the Scripture} [Al-Ma’idah: 5] The verse. And His saying: {Those who disbelieved from among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not separated} [Al-Bayyinah: 1].
And things like that.

The oppressor is unjust by abandoning what has become clear to him of truth and following what has become clear to him that it is falsehood, and speaking without knowledge, so when it appears to him If he turns away from the truth, he is unjust.

This is an example of the fiercest in a quarrel. God Almighty said: {And among the people is he whose speech about the life of this world amazes you, and he calls God to witness of what is in his heart. And He is the most bitter of adversaries.” [Al-Baqarah: 204].
And He said: {They dispute with you about the truth after it has become clear} [Al-Anfal: 6].
And he said: {Here you are, you have argued about what you have knowledge of, so why do you argue about what you have no knowledge} [Al Imran: 66].

chapters.title: Chapter: Islam is the religion of all the prophets
paragraphs: [Chapter: Islam is the religion of all the prophets]
And their saying: He did not say: Be Muslims to him, but by us, that is, on his behalf and on behalf of the Arabs who followed him, and when he brought it and mentioned it in his book.

Then it will be said to them: This and its counterparts are the speech of one who does not understand the Qur’an, and even does not understand the speech of all people, for if it is known from the author of a book he says It was sent down from God, or he says that he classified it as that he calls a people with many clear words and apparent clear deeds. His silence regarding their supplication in some words did not contradict their supplication for him.

But if he is wise in his words, then remaining silent about their supplication in some situations is a wisdom appropriate to that, and this is like His - the Most High - saying: {Say Do you dispute with us about God, when He is our Lord and your Lord, and We have our works and you have your works, and we are sincere to Him?} [Al-Baqarah: 139].

Did he not think that when he commanded his nation to say, “And We are sincere to Him” [Al-Baqarah: 139], the People of the Book were not commanded to be sincere to God, and He He mentioned the command of the People of the Book to be sincere in more than one place, as God Almighty says: {And those who were given the Book did not separate except after it had come to them. Clear evidence} [Al-Bayyinah: 4] (4) {And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion, being true to Islam, and to establish prayer and pay zakat, and that is the religion of value.} [Al-Bayyinah: 5].

Likewise, he called them to Islam and threatened them to turn away from him, such as: {Allah bears witness that there is no god but Him and the angels. And the possessors of knowledge are upholders of justice. There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise.} [Al Imran: 18] (18) {Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam, and those who have been given do not differ. The Book except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves. And whoever disbelieves in the verses of God, then surely God is quick in reckoning.} [Al Imran:

19] (19) {And if they dispute with you, then say, “I have submitted my face to Allah and to those who follow me, and say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered people, ‘Have you submitted?’” Indeed, they are rightly guided, and if they turn away, then it is your responsibility only to convey the message, and God is All-Seeing of His servants} [Al-Imran: 20], and He - the Most High - said:

{And who would turn away from the religion of Abraham except one who fools himself? And We have chosen him in this world, and indeed in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous.} [Al-Baqarah: 130] (130) {When his Lord said to him, “Submit.” He said, “I have submitted to the Lord of the Worlds.” [Al-Baqarah: 131] (131) {And He enjoined it upon Abraham upon his sons, and upon Jacob, “O my son. Indeed, God He has chosen for you the religion, so do not die unless you have submitted.} [Al-Baqarah: 132] (132) {Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, “What “Will you worship someone after me?” They said, “We worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac, one God, and to Him we submit.” [Al-Baqarah: 133].

God, Glory be to Him, has made it clear that no one deviates from the religion of Abraham except one who makes himself foolish, that is, he makes himself foolish, that is, his soul is foolish and ignorant. This is the more correct of the two opinions on this matter, and it is the view of the Kufan grammarians. They allow the directive of distinction to be knowledge, just as it is An indefinite article, then it was reported about him that: {When his Lord said to him, “Submit.” He said, “I have submitted to the Lord of the Worlds” [Al-Baqarah: 131].

He mentioned that Abraham recommended it to his sons, and Jacob also recommended it to his sons. They both said to their sons: “O my son, God has chosen for you the religion.” Do not die unless you are Muslims.} [Al-Baqarah: 132].

Then he mentioned that Jacob upon his death: {When he said to his sons, “What will you worship after me?” They said, “We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham.” Ishmael and Isaac are one God, and to Him we submit.” [Al-Baqarah: 133].

These are Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob, all of them following Islam, and they were enjoining Islam. Then he said after that: {And they say, “Be Jews or Christians, and you will be guided.” Say, “Rather, the religion of Abraham is upright, and he was not of the polytheists.” [Al-Baqarah: 135].

Then he said: {Say, “We believe in God and in what was revealed to us, and what was revealed to Abraham, and Ishmael, and Isaac, and Jacob, and the tribes, and what was given to Moses.” And Jesus and what was given to the prophets from their Lord - We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit.} [Al-Baqarah: 136].

Then he said: {And if they believe in the same as you have believed, then they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, then they are only in discord, then God will suffice for them, and He is the Hearer. The All-Knowing} [Al-Baqarah: 137].

He has informed that if they turn away from believing in the same manner as you believed in, which includes your saying: And to Him we submit, then they are only in Dissension, that is: opponents of Allah and His Messenger, as God Almighty said: {It is He who brought out those who disbelieved from the People of the Book from their homes at the beginning of the gathering. You thought that they would go out, and they thought that their strongholds would protect them from God, so God came to them from where they had not expected, and cast terror into their hearts. They destroy their homes with their own hands and with the hands of the believers. So consider, O you who have sight.} [Al-Hashr: 2].
To his saying: {That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger, and whoever opposes Allah - surely Allah is severe in punishment} [Al-Hashr: 4].

And His saying - the Almighty -: {And We submit to Him} [Al-Baqarah: 133] in the spider, is like His saying: {And We submit to Him} [Al-Baqarah: 133] in Al-Baqarah with their call to Islam, and likewise in Surat Al Imran in its saying: {Say, O People of the Book, come to a common word between us. And among you is that we shall worship none but God, nor associate anything with Him, nor take one another as lords besides God. But if they turn away, then say, “Bear witness that Muslims} [Al Imran: 64].

He first called them to Islam, which is the worship of God alone, with no partner, and not to take one another as lords without God, as God Almighty said: {They took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God and the Messiah, son of Mary, and they were not commanded except to worship a god. One, there is no god but Him. Glory be to Him above what they associate with Him.} [At-Tawbah: 31].
Then He Almighty said: {But if they turn away, say: Bear witness that we are Muslims} [Al Imran: 64].
This is the verse that the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - wrote to Caesar, the king of the Romans, when he invited him to Islam.
He said in his book.

“In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, from Muhammad, the Messenger of God, to Heraclius, the Great of Rome, peace be upon whoever follows guidance. As for what follows: I invite you With the call to Islam, submit and you will be safe. Submit and God will give you your reward twice. And if you turn back, then upon you is only the sin of the Arisians and: {O People of the Book, come to a common word between us and you: that we worship none but Allah, and do not associate anything with Him, and do not take lords other than Allah. But if they turn away, then say, “Bear witness that we submit.” [Al Imran: 64] »

So the Prophet called him to Islam, in the letter that he sent to him, and he also said in the family of Imran: {It is not for a human being that God should give him the Book and the judgment. And prophecy. Then He says to the people, “Be my servants instead of God, but be divine in that you teach the Scripture and in that you study.” [Al-Bukhari and Muslim] Al-Imran: 79] (79) {And he does not command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Does he command you to disbelieve after you have submitted?} [Al-Imran: 80] .

So he mentioned monotheism in this verse, and he declared a disbeliever who takes the angels and the prophets as lords, so what about he who takes the rabbis and monks? lords. Then he mentioned belief in the Seal of the Messengers, and said: {And when God took a covenant from the prophets: “I have given you of the Book and of wisdom. Then there came to you a Messenger.” Confirming what is with you, that you may believe in it and support it. He said, “Have you affirmed, and you have taken my pledge?” They said, “We affirm.” He said, “Then bear witness, and I.” With you among the witnesses} [Al Imran: 81] (81) {But whoever turns away after that - those are the transgressors} [Al Imran:

82] (82) {Is it that other than the religion of Allah they seek, when to Him have surrendered whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and to Him they will be returned} [Al Imran: 83] (83) {Say, “We believe.” By God and what was revealed to us and what was sent down to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets. Their Lord, We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit.} [Al Imran: 84] (84) {And whoever desires other than Islam as a religion, it will not be accepted from him while he is in The Hereafter is among the losers} [Al Imran: 85].

He mentioned that he made a covenant with the prophets and their nations: Whatever book and wisdom I give you, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you. That you may believe in him and support him.

This indicates the matter for all the People of the Book, if a second messenger comes to them, to believe in him and support him, even if they have among them The Book and the wisdom did not happen, and they do not say: We are self-sufficient with what we have of the Book and the wisdom. We do not believe in the Messenger who came to us.

We limit faith to Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - because he is the seal of the messengers, and he is the last messenger to come confirming what was before him of the Book, so it is obligatory. Whoever comes to him must believe in him and support him, even if he has the Book and wisdom, whatever that is.
And this covenant God took from the prophets, and they took it from their nations, then He said: {Is it the religion of Allah that they seek?} [Al Imran: 83].

This is the religion of God with which He sent His messengers and sent down His books. So whoever seeks something other than it has sought other than the religion of God, and it is the religion. Islam, (which He said) about it: {And whoever desires a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers} [Al Imran: 85].

chapters.title: Detailing the command of believers to speak the truth so that it can be used as evidence against the one who opposes it
paragraphs: [Chapter: Commanding the believers to speak the truth so that the argument can be established against the dissenter.]

As for His saying - the Most High -: {And do not dispute with the People of the Book except in a way that is best, except with those of them who are unjust. And say, “We believe in that which has been revealed to us.” And it was revealed to you, and our God and your God are One, and to Him we submit.} [Al-Ankabut: 46].

It is a command for the believers to speak the truth that God has made obligatory upon them, and upon all creation, in order to please God thereby, and to establish the argument against Him. Those who disagree, for this is part of the argument that is better, which is to say something that is true and obliges you, and the one who is disputing with you is obligated to say it. If he agrees with you, otherwise his stubbornness and injustice will appear.

As God Almighty said in the other verse: “Say, ‘Do you dispute with us about God when He is our Lord and your Lord? We have our works and you have your works and we belong to Him. Sincere} [Al-Baqarah: 139].
For we are in common that He is the Lord of us all, and that the work of every worker belongs to Him and no one else.

We have the advantage that we are loyal to Him, and you are not sincere to Him. This necessitated that the truth is with us and not you, and that our deeds Good deeds are accepted, and your deeds will be rejected.

This is similar to His saying - the Almighty -: {Say, O People of the Book, come to a common word between us and you: that we worship none but Allah, and that we associate no partners with Him. Nothing in it, and do not take one another as lords other than Allah. But if they turn away, then say, “Bear witness that we are Muslims.” [Al Imran: 64].
So His command to them to say, “Bear witness that we are Muslims” included establishing the proof against them, as Christ - peace be upon him - used to say.

chapters.title: A chapter refuting their claim is that injustice characterized the Jews rather than the Christians
paragraphs: [Chapter: Refuting their claim that injustice characterized the Jews rather than the Christians]
Then they said:

As for those who did wrong, no one doubts that they are the Jews who prostrated themselves before the head of the calf, and disbelieved in God many times, not just one time. And they killed his prophets and apostles, and worshiped idols, and sacrificed to devils, not only inanimate animals, but also their sons and daughters according to what God bore witness against them, saying, through the mouth of David the Prophet - peace be upon him - in the Book of the Psalms in Psalm 115, saying: They slaughtered their sons and their daughters. to demons, and they shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters who were sacrificed to the graven images in Canaan, and the land was defiled with their blood, and was defiled. Their deeds were adulterous, according to their malice, and the LORD was angry with them, and despised their inheritance.

He also said through the mouth of the Prophet Isaiah - peace be upon him - God says about the children of Israel: They have not obeyed my commandments, they have not kept everything that I have commanded them. With it,
Rather, they changed and broke the covenant that I had made with them forever. Therefore I made them sit with grief, and destroyed them, and the Of those among whom joy and happiness remain.

Thus says God concerning the inhabitants of the Holy House of the children of Israel: I will scatter them among the nations, and in those days they will exalt the nations. They will raise their voices and praise God and glorify Him with loud voices, and they will gather from the ends of the earth, from the isles of the sea, and from the countries far away, and they will sanctify the name of God and return to God, the God of Israel, and they will be a people, but the children of Israel will be scattered throughout The earth.

And the Prophet Isaiah - peace be upon him - said: God says: (O children of Israel, you have defiled my holy mountain, for I will consume you with war, and you will die. This is because I called you and you did not answer, and I spoke to you and you did not listen, and you did the thing before me.)

Isaiah also said: “Indeed, God has hated the children of Israel, and has expelled them from their homes and from his house, and will not forgive them because they are a curse. And they were made the curse of mankind. Therefore God destroyed them and scattered them among the nations. He will no longer have mercy on them nor look upon them with mercy forever. For ever and ever, and they will not offer an offering or a sacrifice to God in that day or that time, nor will the children of Israel rejoice, because they have strayed from God - the Almighty -).

The Prophet Jeremiah - peace be upon him - said: (Just as the Ethiopian cannot be white, so the children of Israel cannot abandon their custom. The evil nation, and for this reason I have no mercy, nor pity, nor pity toward the evil nation, nor do I pity it.)

The Prophet Ezekiel - peace be upon him - said: (God said: I only lifted up My hand from the children of Israel and scattered them among the nations, because they did not My commandments, and they did not obey my commands, and they disobeyed me in them, and what I said to them, and they did not listen to me.)

There are many sayings like this in the Torah, the books of the prophets, and the Psalms of David. The Jews recite them in their churches and recite them. They do not deny a single word of it, and it is the same as it is with them, and it is the same with us in all tongues.
The answer is to say:

As for the fact that the Jews were wrongdoers, unbelievers, and transgressors, deserving of God’s punishment and punishment, this is clearly known from the religion of Muhammad. Copied Repeatedly, as it was known by necessity and the recurrent transmission from him - may God bless him and grant him peace - that the Christians are also unjust, aggressors, and disbelievers. They are deserving of God’s punishment and punishment, and in the Jews there is disbelief that is not in the Christians, and in the Christians there is what is not in the Jews, for the Jews changed The law of the Torah before the Messiah, son of Mary, came to them. When he came to them, they disbelieved in him and denied him. When Muhammad was sent, they rejected him, so they became angry. In anger.

As God Almighty said about them: “Do you believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part? Then what is the recompense for those of you who do that except disgrace in life of this world and on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned to the severest of torment, and God is not unaware of what you do.} [Al-Baqarah: 85] (85) Those are the ones who bought The life of this world is replaced by the Hereafter, so the torment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be helped.} [Al-Baqarah:

86] (86) {And We gave Moses the Scripture, and followed him with messengers, and We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs, and supported him with the Holy Spirit. Did you speak? There has come to you a messenger with that which your souls do not desire. You were arrogant, so a group you denied, and a group you killed.} [Al-Baqarah: 87] (87) {And they said, “Our hearts are uncircumcised.” God has cursed them for their disbelief, so little do they believe} [Al-Baqarah: 88] (88) {And when there came to them a book from God, confirming what is with them, and they were of the past They seek victory against those who disbelieve, but when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers} [Al-Baqarah:

89] (89) {Evil is what they sold their souls for. So they unleashed anger upon anger, and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment} [Al-Baqarah: 90] (90) {And when it is said to them, “Believe in what God has revealed,” they say, “We believe in what was revealed.” upon Us, and disbelieve in what is behind it, while it is the truth, confirming what is with them. Say, “Why did you kill God’s prophets before, if you were believers?” [Al-Baqarah: 91] (91) {And Moses came to you with clear proofs, then you took the calf after him, and you were wrongdoers} [Al-Baqarah:

92] (92) {And when We took a covenant with you and raised above you the Mount: “Take what We have given you firmly and listen.” They said, “We hear, but we disobey.” And drink in it. Their hearts are hasty because of their disbelief. Say: “Wretched is that which your faith commands you, if you are believers” [Al-Baqarah: 93].
So he became angry with them, first by denying Christ, and second by denying Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace.

And He, the Almighty, said: {Humility has been inflicted upon them wherever they find themselves, except with a rope from God and a rope from mankind, and they have incurred the wrath of God, and it has been inflicted upon them. This is because they used to disbelieve in the verses of God and kill the prophets unjustly. This is because they disobeyed and transgressed} [Al- Imran: 112].

And God Almighty said: {Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel on the tongue of David and Jesus son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and used to transgress.} [Al-Ma’idah: 78] (78) {They did not refrain from an evil which they did; evil was what they did} [Al-Maeda: 79].

And He Almighty said: {Say, “Shall I inform you of any evil like that as a reward from God?” He whom God has cursed and become angry with and made among them apes and swine. And he worshiped the tyrant} [Al-Maeda: 60].

So it became clear that the Jews were cursed by God and that they worshiped the tyrant, and that He made apes and pigs of them, and something like this is in the Qur’an. Many, but the speaker says that they are what is meant by His saying - the Most High -: {Except those among them who do wrong} [Al-Baqarah: 150].
In his saying: {And do not dispute with the People of the Book except in a way that is best, except with those who are unjust among them} [Al-Ankabut: 46].
A clear mistake, and that is why it was invalid by Muslim agreement.
For God Almighty says: {And do not dispute with the People of the Book except in a way that is best} [Al-Ankabut: 46].
It is forbidden to argue with the People of the Book, whether Jews or Christians, except in what is best.
And His saying: {Except those who do wrong} [Al-Baqarah: 150].
From all sects.

For this reason, it is obligatory upon the Muslims, if a Jew and a Christian argue with them, to argue with him in a way that is best, except for the one who is unjust. The two sects, for he is punished sometimes with the tongue and with the hand at other times, just as God and His Messenger commanded jihad against the oppressors among these, so the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace Peace and blessings of God be upon him - the Jews who were in the Prophet’s city and around it and near it, just as the Banu Qaynuqa’, al-Nadir, and Qurayza jihad. The people of Khaybar, the people of Wadi Al-Qura, and others.

Just as he fought against the Christians in the year of Tabuk, he invaded them in the Levant, Arabs and Romans, and his deputies invaded them before that: Zaid bin Haritha and Jafar. Ibn Abi Talib and Abdullah Ibn Rawaha, and he ordered them to invade them, and his Rightly Guided Caliphs invaded them after him.

When the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - came to Najran, the Christian delegation argued with them in his mosque in a way that was best, then God - Glory be to Him - commanded him - To invite them to the mubahala, so they abstained from it, and agreed to pay the jizyah by hand while they were young, as was mentioned in detail. Some of them argued in a way that was best, and the oppressor among them punished him and fought against him, just as he punished the oppressor among the Jews.

Among the most astonishing things is their saying: As for those who did wrong, no one doubts that they are the Jews, for this is of the same nature as their saying: Then We found in the Book something greater than this as proof, and it is its saying in Surat Al-Shura: {And say, “I believe in what God has sent down of the Book, and I have been commanded.” That God, our Lord and your Lord, will be just between you. We have our deeds and you have your deeds.} [Al-Shura: 15] as mentioned above.

It is of the same type as their saying in His saying: {This is the Book in which there is no doubt, a guidance for the righteous, who believe in the unseen and establish prayer, and from what We have provided for them, and they spend.} [Al-Baqarah: 2].

By the Book he meant the Gospel, and those who believe in the unseen: the Christians, and those who believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you are Muslims, and their claim that this is clear and apparent.

The Christian interpretations of the divine books contain distortion of the words of God, and atheism in the names of God and His verses, which is described for a long time and will never end. It is astonishing at him, but their attempt to interpret the Qur’an with atheism and distortion is more astonishing and more astonishing, such as their saying: [Indeed, Muhammad - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him And he greeted - he mentioned that he was not sent to them, and that he praised the religion they followed after abrogation and alteration, after he was sent - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. And peace be upon him -, and his saying {the path of those whom You have bestowed} [Al-Fatihah: 7] meant the Christians.
And his saying: “Indeed, We have sent Our messengers” [Al-Hadid: 25] meant the disciples.
And His saying: {And He sent down with them the Book with truth that He might judge between the people} [Al-Baqarah: 213].

He meant the Gospel] This is an apparent lie and slander against Muhammad that he wanted these things. Their slander against the prophets, because they reported that Christ is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and that the Torah, the Psalms, and other The books told about that, then they come to what every rational person knows that Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - did not want it, and they say:

No one doubts it, and it is a clear and clear statement, and everyone who knows the condition of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and what he brought from the Qur’an Religion knows with certain and necessary knowledge that Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - did not make the Christians believers rather than the Jews, but rather he used to disbelieve The two sects, and he commands their jihad, and declares a disbeliever who does not consider their jihad obligatory for him.

This is what the Muslims have agreed upon, and it is transmitted to them from their Prophet on a frequent basis. Rather, this is known from its appropriate condition. And the one who opposes, except for one who is extremely ignorant of his condition, or one who is apparently stubborn and obstinate.

chapters.title: So Muslims agreed with the Christians in what the Jews disbelieved in
paragraphs: [Chapter: The Muslims agree with the Christians in what they disbelieved in the Jews]

As for what they reported from the prophets, which indicates the disbelief of the Jews, this is something we do not dispute with them, and there is no need for us to infer anything. They transmitted it, even though there is in what is proven from the prophets something that shows their disbelief when they changed the religion of Moses - peace be upon him - just as the Christians disbelieved when they changed the religion Christ, this is a truth that agrees with what the Seal of the Messengers - may God bless him and grant him peace - told us. We know their disbelief from a point of view that we do not doubt. Believe it.

And what they told us about the prophets, if we knew that they were truthful in it, we believed them in it, and if we knew that they lied in it, we would deny them in it, and if we did not We know whether he is truthful or a lie. We do not believe him and do not disbelieve in him. Rather, we say: {We believe in what was revealed to us and what was revealed to you, and our God and your God. One, and to Him we submit.} [Al-Ankabut: 46].

Belief in all that was given to the prophets is a right and an obligation, but the obligation of believing in the specific prophet whom we did not know from anyone else rests on two premises: 1 - That the word was said by the Prophet 2 - And that the meaning with which they interpreted it meant the Prophet who spoke that statement, so it must be proven Attribution and significance of the text.
These two introductions are essential in everything transmitted from the prophets.

It may be necessary for a third introduction for those who did not know the Hebrew language, as Moses, David, Christ, and others only spoke In the Hebrew language, whoever does not know it, but only knows Arabic or Roman, must know that the translator is from those The language to this has been translated identically.

chapters.title: Chapter on the Christian exaggeration regarding Jesus, the servant of God and His Messenger
paragraphs: [Chapter: The Christians’ exaggeration regarding Jesus, the servant of God and His Messenger]

As for their saying: As for us Christians, we did not do anything that the Jews did, so it is said to them: Disbelief, immorality, and disobedience did not It is limited to the sins of the Jews. If you do not do the same as their deeds, then you will have words and deeds, some of which are greater than the disbelief of the Jews. And if you are gentler than the Jews and closer in affection, then you are also more ignorant and misguided than the Jews.

And He - the Almighty - said: {And they say: The Most Gracious has taken a son} [Maryam: 88] (88) {Indeed, you have come to something bitter} [Maryam: 89] (89) {The heavens are almost bursting with water from it. And the earth will split open, and the mountains will fall down in ruins.} [Maryam: 90] (90) {Indeed, they called for the Most Merciful a son} [Maryam: 91] (91) {And it is not appropriate for the Most Merciful to take sons} [Maryam: 92] (92) {Indeed, everyone in the heavens and the earth except one who comes to the Most Gracious is a servant} [Maryam: 93] (93) {Indeed, He has numbered them and numbered them as a number} [Maryam: 94] (94) {And they will all come to Him alone on the Day of Resurrection} [Maryam: 95] And He - the Most High - said: {Praise be to God who sent down to His servant the Book and did not make for himself crooked} [Al-Kahf:

1] (1) {Righteous, to warn of severe punishment from Himself, and to give good news to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward} [Al-Kahf: 2] (2) {Remaining Therein forever.} [Al-Kahf: 3] (3) And He warns those who say, “God has taken a son.” [Al-Kahf: 4] (4) “They have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers. It comes out of their mouths. They say nothing but a lie.} [Al-Kahf: 5].

And God Almighty said: {Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day, and do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not follow the religion of truth. Those who were given the Book until they were given the tribute with help, but they were humble.} [At-Tawbah: 29].

And He Almighty said: {And the Jews said, “Uzair is the son of God,” and the Christians said, “The Messiah is the son of God.” That is what they say with their mouths, imitating the words of Those who disbelieved before - God killed them. How can they be saved?} [At-Tawbah: 30] (30) {They took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God, and the Messiah is the son of Maryam, and they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no god but Him. Glory be to Him above what they associate with Him.” [At-Tawbah: 31].

And He - the Almighty - said: {They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, but God refuses except to perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it - It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, to make it prevail over all religions, even though the polytheists dislike it - O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis And the monks devour people’s wealth unjustly and avert from the path of God.} [At-Tawbah: 32-34].

And God Almighty said: {And among those who said, “Indeed, we are Christians.” We took a covenant from them, but they forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of, so We enticed among them enmity. And hatred will last until the Day of Resurrection, and God will inform them of what they used to do.” [Al-Ma’idah: 14].

And He - the Almighty - said: When he narrated the story of the Messiah - peace be upon him -: {That is Jesus, son of Mary. He spoke the truth about which they dispute} [Maryam: 34] (34) {Whatever God may take from him a son. Glory be to Him. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, “Be,” and it is.} [Maryam: 35] (35) {And indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord. So worship Him. This is a straight path.} [Maryam: 36] (36) {Then the factions differed from among them. So woe to those who disbelieved at the sight of a terrible day} [Maryam: 37] (37) {Listen to them and see on the Day they come to Us, but the wrongdoers today are in clear error} [Maryam: 38].

And He Almighty said: {Say, “O People of the Book, do not go to extremes in your religion other than the truth, and do not follow the desires of a people who had gone astray before, and had misled many.” And they have strayed from the right path} [Al-Maeda: 77].

chapters.title: Separating the extremism of Jews and Christians and the mediation of Muslims
paragraphs: [Chapter: Extremism of Jews and Christians and Moderation of Muslims]

Whoever ponders the situation of the Jews and Christians with the Muslims, he will find the Jews and Christians facing each other, these on one side of error, and those on the other side. He opposes him, and Muslims are the middle.
This applies to monotheism, the prophets, laws, what is permissible and what is forbidden, morals, and other things.

The Jews liken the Creator to the created being with regard to the imperfect qualities specific to the created thing, which the Lord, Glory be to Him, must be distanced from, as the saying of the one who said: Some of them said: He is poor, and he is stingy, and he labored when he created the heavens and the earth, and the Christians liken the creation to the Creator in terms of his attributes. The perfection that pertains to the Creator, to which there is no equal, such as their saying that Christ is God and the Son of God.
Each of the two statements requires the other.

Christians also describe theology with the attributes of imperfection from which the Lord must be distanced, and they curse God in a way that no human being has ever reviled Him. Just as Muadh bin Jabal used to say: Do not have mercy on them, for they have reviled God in a way that no human being has ever reviled.
The Jews claim that God forbids from abrogating what He has legislated, just as He forbids what does not fall within His power or contradicts knowledge and wisdom.

The Christians permitted their elders to abrogate the law of God with which He sent His messengers, so they made lawful what was forbidden, just as they made lawful the pig and other things. They did not forbid anything, but they forbade what was permissible, just as they forbade in their monasticism which they invented, and they forbade in it some good things. God made it permissible, and they omitted what was obligatory just as they omitted circumcision and other things, and they omitted the types of purification such as washing, removing impurity and other things. That.
They oblige what was omitted, just as they obligated from the laws what God and His prophets did not oblige.

The Muslims described the Lord with the perfect attributes that He deserves, and that He is free from imperfection, and that He has an example, so they described Him with what He was described with. himself, and as his messengers described him without distortion or obstruction, without adaptation or imitation, even though they knew that he was not like him. Something neither in itself, nor in its attributes, nor in its actions.

And they said: Indeed, to Him belongs the creation and the command. Just as He creates no one else, He does not command anyone else. Rather, all religion belongs to Him. He is the worshiped, obedient one who does not No one deserves worship except Him, and there is no obedience to anyone except obedience to Him, and He abrogates whatever of His law He abrogates, and no one else has the right to abrogate His law.

The Jews went to extremes in avoiding impurities and prohibiting good things, and the Christians made permissible the impurities and wearing impurities, and the Muslims made it permissible God grants them the good things, unlike the Jews, and forbids them the bad things, unlike the Christians.

The Jews exaggerate the purity of their bodies despite the impurity of their hearts, while the Christians claim that they purify their hearts despite the impurity. Their bodies, and Muslims purify all their bodies and hearts.
The Christians have acts of worship and morals, but no knowledge, no knowledge, and no intelligence, and the Jews have intelligence, noesis, and no knowledge, no acts of worship. Good morals.

Muslims combined useful knowledge and good deeds, zakat and intelligence, for God sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth. Guidance includes useful knowledge, and the religion of truth includes good deeds to make them prevail over all religions, and manifestation is through knowledge and the tongue to make it clear. It is truth and guidance, and it is with the hand and weapons to be a victor and supporter, and God made this appearance appear to him, for they are the people of the straight path. The path of those upon whom God has bestowed blessings, of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. The truth, and they do not act upon it, like the Jews, nor do they go astray who work, worship, and renounce without knowledge, like the Christians.
The Jews killed the prophets, and those who command justice from the people, and the Christians took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God. And the Messiah, the son of Mary.

And the Muslims were moderate and believed in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers, and they did not differentiate between any of His messengers, and they believed in all the prophets. And with every book that God has sent down, they did not deny the prophets, nor did they curse them, nor did they go to extremes in them, nor did they worship them. And so do the people of knowledge and religion. They deprive them of their rights and do not go to extremes in them.
The Jews are angry for themselves and take revenge, while the Christians are not angry with their Lord nor take revenge.

And the moderate Muslims who follow their Prophet are angry with their Lord and pardon their misfortunes, as in the two Sahihs on the authority of Aisha - may God be pleased with her. On her authority - that she said: “The Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - never struck with his hand any of his servants, or a woman, or anything, unless he was struggling in God’s path, and nothing has ever happened to him so he avenges himself, unless God’s prohibitions are violated and he avenges God.”

And in the two Sahih books on the authority of Anas bin Malik - may God be pleased with him - he said: “I served the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - for ten years, but he did not say to me: ‘Ugh. He never said to me about something I did: Why did I do it? Nor for anything I did not do: Why did you not do it? Whenever some of his family blamed me for something, he would say: “Leave him, for if anything were settled, it would be done.”

This is in his own right, and as for the limits of God, in the two Sahih books on the authority of Aisha - may God be pleased with her -: “(The Quraysh were concerned about the matter of The Makhzoumiyah that had been stolen, so they said: Who will speak to the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace -? (So they said: Who can dare about it except Usama bin Zayd? The love of the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace -) Then Usama spoke to him about it and said:

O Osama, do I intercede for one of the punishments imposed by God? Those before you were destroyed because if a noble person among them stole, they would abandon him, and if he stole Among them is the weak, and they impose punishments on him, and by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if Fatima, the daughter of Muhammad, had stolen, I would have cut off her hand.”

God has described the nation of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - as the most beneficial of nations to creation, and He said: {You are the best nation ever brought forth for the people, commanding people. And you do what is right and forbid what is wrong and you believe in God. And if the People of the Book had believed, it would have been better for them than the believers, and most of them The defiantly disobedient} [Al Imran: 110].

In the nation of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - the enjoining of what is right and the forbidding of what is evil entails the well-being of the servants in this life and the hereafter, unless There is something like it in both nations.

chapters.title: The chapter refuting the Christians’ claim is that the Qur’an denies polytheism from them
paragraphs: [Chapter: Refuting the Christians’ claim that the Qur’an denied them polytheism]

Then they said: And likewise it came in this book, saying: {You will find that the most intense of people in hostility to those who believe are the Jews and those who associate others; and you will find The closest in affection to those who believe are those who say, “Indeed, we are Christians.” That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant.} [Al-Ma’idah: 82].

So he mentioned the priests and monks, lest it be said: This was said about others, and this indicated our actions and good intentions, and denied the name polytheism. By saying: The Jews and those who associate polytheists are the most hostile of people to those who believe, and those who say, “We are Christians” are the closest in affection.

The answer is to say: The complete speech: {And when they hear what was revealed to the Messenger, you will see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized. Our Lord, we believed, so record us with the witnesses, and what do we have? We do not believe in God and the truth that has come to us, and we hope that our Lord will admit us with the righteous people. So God rewarded them for what they said, with Gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. And that is the reward of the doers of good.} [Al-Maeda: 83]

He, Glory be to Him, has not promised reward in the Hereafter except to those who believed in Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - about whom He said: {And when They heard what was revealed to the Messenger. You will see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they recognized of the truth. They say, “Our Lord, we believe, so record us with the witnesses.” [Al-Maeda: 83].

And the witnesses are those who bore witness to his message and testified that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they The martyrs about whom He said: {And thus We have made you a moderate nation that you may be witnesses over the people and that the Messenger may be a witness over you} [Al-Baqarah: 143].
For this reason, Ibn Abbas and others said in his statement: “So write us down with the witnesses” [Al Imran: 53].
He said, “With Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and his nation.”

And everyone who bears witness to the Messengers’ truthfulness is one of the witnesses, as the disciples said: {Our Lord, we have believed in what You have sent down, and we have followed the Messenger, so record us with The two witnesses} [Al Imran: 53].

And He Almighty said: {O you who have believed, bow down and prostrate and worship your Lord and do good that you may succeed} [Al-Hajj: 77] (77) {And strive in God's struggle is true. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in religion any hardship to the religion of your father Abraham. He has called you Muslims before and in this. So that the Messenger may be a witness over you, and that you may be witnesses over the people} [Al-Hajj: 78].

As for his saying at the beginning of the verse: {You will find that the most intense of the people in hostility to those who believe are the Jews and those who associate polytheists, and you will find the closest of them in affection. For those who believe, those who say, “Indeed, we are Christians.” [Al-Ma’idah: 82].

It is as He - Glory be to Him - the Most High - informed, that the enmity of the polytheists and the Jews to the believers is more severe than the enmity of the Christians, and the Christians are closer to Out of affection for them, and this is known among the morals of the Jews, for the Jews possess hatred, envy, and enmity that the Christians do not have.
The Christians have mercy and affection that the Jews do not have, and enmity has its root in hatred, for the Jews used to hate their prophets. So how about their hatred for believers?

As for the Christians, there is no enmity or hatred in the religion that they profess towards the enemies of God who waged war against God and His Messenger and striven to spread corruption throughout the earth. So what about their hostility and hatred towards the moderate believers, the people of the religion of Abraham, who believe in all the Scriptures and the Messengers?

This does not mean praising the Christians for their belief in God, nor is it a promise to them of being saved from torment and deserving of reward. Rather, it means that they The closest affection, and His Almighty says: {That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant} [Al-Ma’idah: 82].

That is, because of these people, and because of abandoning arrogance, a kind of affection develops among them, which makes them better than the polytheists and closer to affection. From Jews and polytheists.
Then He Almighty said: {And when they hear what was sent down to the Messenger, you will see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth} [Al-Maeda: 83].

These are the ones whom He praised for their faith and promised them the reward of the Hereafter, and the conscience, even if it refers to the predecessors, then what is meant is the race of the predecessors, not all of them. One of them, as God Almighty says: “Those to whom the people said, ‘Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them.’ It increased their faith, and they said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us.’” And He is the best disposer of affairs} [Al Imran: 173].

It is as if the race of people, they said to them: The race of people, they have been collected, but the generality refrains, for the one who said is from the people, and the one to whom it is said is from the people, and the one being said On his behalf from the people, and it is impossible for all the people to say to all the people: He has gathered all the people for you.
An example of that is His saying - the Almighty -: {And the Jews said: Uzair is the son of God} [At-Tawbah: 30].

Which type of Jews said this, not every Jew said this, and from this is that the Christians have a gentleness of heart that obligates them to believe in something that is not In the Jews, and this is true, and as for their saying: He denied us the name polytheism, there is no doubt that God differentiated between the polytheists and the People of the Book in several matters. places, and described those among them who were polytheists in some places. Rather, he distinguished between the Sabians and the Magians and between the polytheists in some places, and both Both matters are true. The first is like His - Most High - saying: {Those who disbelieve are not among the People of the Book and the polytheists} [Al-Bayyinah: 1].
And He - the Most High - said: {Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians, and the Magians, and those who associate others} [Al-Hajj: 17].
And He - the Almighty - said: {You will find that the most intense of people in hostility to those who believe are the Jews and those who associate others with others} [Al-Maeda: 82].

As for describing them as polytheists, it is in His saying: {They took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God and the Messiah, the son of Mary, and they were not commanded. Except that they worship One God; there is no god but Him. Glory be to Him above what they associate with Him.} [At-Tawbah: 31].

So he distanced himself from their polytheism, and that is because the origin of their religion does not contain polytheism, for God only sent His messengers with monotheism and forbidding Polytheism, as God Almighty said: {And ask of those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: We have made gods to be worshiped, besides the Most Gracious} [Al-Zukhruf: 45].
And He - the Almighty - said: {And We have certainly sent into every nation a messenger, saying, “Worship God and avoid the tyrant” [An-Nahl: 36].
And He - the Almighty - said: {And We did not send before you any messenger but to him was it revealed that there is no god but Me, so worship Me} [Al-Anbiya’: 25].

The Messiah, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and the messengers before him only called to worship God alone, without any partner, and in the Torah it is That is what is great in his description. None of the prophets commanded that an angel, nor a prophet, nor a star, nor an idol be worshiped, nor that one should be asked or requested. Intercession to God for the dead or the absent, neither a prophet nor an angel. None of the messengers were commanded to call the angels and say: Intercede for us. God does not invite the prophets and the righteous, the dead or those who are absent, and He says:

Intercede on our behalf with God, and let not their statues be depicted, neither in the form of a shadow, nor depicted in the walls, nor by making a supplication of their statues and venerating them. closeness and obedience, whether they intended to supplicate the owners of the statues, glorify them and seek their intercession, and asked them to ask God Almighty, They made those statues a reminder of their owners, or they intended to pray to the statues, but they did not realize that

What is meant is the supplication of its companions, as the ignorant polytheists did, even if that is all in all of this. They are only worshiping Satan, even if they do not They intend to worship Him, for He may appear to them in an image that they think is the image of the One whom they venerate, and say: I am Al-Khidr, I am the Messiah, I am Girgis, I am Sheikh So-and-so.

This also happened to more than one of those affiliated with the Muslims and Christians, and Satan may enter some of the statues and speak to them. It may fulfill some of their needs. For this reason and others like it, polytheism has appeared in ancient and modern times, and Christians and their ilk did the polytheism they did.

As for the prophets and messengers - may God’s prayers and peace be upon them - they forbade all of this, and none of them legislated any of that. The Christians do not command the veneration of embodied idols, but rather the veneration of pictorial statues. They are not following pure monotheism, and they are not Like the polytheists who worship idols and deny messengers. For this reason, God made them a type of non-polytheists at times, and condemned them for what they said. Sometimes they caused him to abandon polytheism.

And when the term “polytheism” is used, a group of Muslims includes all the disbelievers from the People of the Book, and others, as He Almighty says: {And Marry polytheist women until they believe, and a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist woman, even if she pleases you, and do not marry polytheist women until they believe.” [Al-Baqarah: 221].

Among the people are those who make the term general for all infidels, especially the Christians. Then there are those who forbid the marriage of these people, as Abd Allah Ibn Umar forbade the marriage of a Christian woman, and said: I do not know of greater polytheism than saying: Jesus is her Lord.
This is the opinion of a group of Shiites and others.

As for the majority of the predecessors and successors, they permitted the marriage of women of the Book and permitted their sacrifices, but if they said the word “polytheists” is general, they said: This verse is specific to or abrogated by the verse about the table, which is His saying - the Most High -: {And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you. And your food is lawful for them, and the chaste women are among the believing women, and the chaste women are among those who were given the Scripture before you, if you give them their wages, being chaste. They are not fornicators or deceivers.} [Al-Ma’idah: 5].
Another sect considers the word “polytheists” to be used in general terms and does not include the People of the Book.

As for the fact that Christians have polytheism, as God mentioned, this is agreed upon among Muslims, as the Qur’an has spoken of it, and Muslims They are agreed that his saying: {You will find the people most intense in hostility to those who believe are the Jews and those who associate polytheists, and you will find the closest of them in affection to those who believe. Those who said, “Indeed, we are Christians.” [Al-Ma’idah: 82].
The Christians are not included in the term “those who associate polytheists” just as they are not included in the term “Jews.”
Likewise, His saying: “Those who disbelieve are not among the People of the Book and the polytheists” [Al-Bayyinah: 1].

And so on. This is because the meaning of a single word varies with its singularity and conjunction, so it includes something that is not It is included in it when combined with something else, like the word good and evil in His saying - the Most High -: {He commands them to do what is right and forbids them from The Munkar} [Al-A’raf: 157].
Here he addresses everything that God has commanded, as it is known, and everything he has forbidden, as it is reprehensible.
And in his saying: {There is no good in much of their private communication, except in the one who enjoins charity, or kindness, or reconciliation between people} [An-Nisa: 114].
Here he linked charity with kindness and reconciliation between people.
The same applies to the evil in his saying: “Indeed, prayer forbids indecency and evil” [Al-Ankabut: 45].

He linked indecency with immorality, and said: “Indeed, God commands justice and goodness and giving to relatives and forbids indecency.” And the abominable and the unjust admonish you that you may remember} [An-Nahl: 90].
He linked indecency with abomination and transgression.

Likewise, the word “righteousness and faith” when used individually includes good deeds and piety, as in His saying: “But righteousness is he who believes in God.” And the Last Day and the angels and the Scripture and the prophets} [Al-Baqarah: 177].
And he said: {Indeed, the righteous are in bliss} [Al-Infitar: 13].

And he said: {The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, are terrified in their hearts, and when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith and in their Lord. They put their trust” [Al-Anfal: 2].
He may associate it with something else, such as His saying: “And cooperate in righteousness and piety” [Al-Ma’idah: 2].
And His saying: {Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds} [Al-Baqarah: 277].
Likewise, the word “faqir” and “al-miskin,” if one of them is used separately, includes the meaning of the other.
He may combine the two in his saying: {The alms are only for the poor and the needy} [Al-Tawbah: 60].

So there are two types here, and in those cases there is one type, and so is the word polytheism in the example of his saying: {The polytheists are only unclean, so do not They will approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs} [At-Tawbah: 28].

All disbelievers, the People of the Book and others according to the general scholars, are included in it because he singled it out and stripped it away, even if they were, when combined with the People of The book was of two types.

And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Buraydah, that the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace -: “Whenever he sent an emir with a convoy, or an army, he commanded him in a special He encouraged himself to fear God, and advised him to be kind to those Muslims with him, and said to them:

Fight in the name of God in the name of God, fight whoever disbelieves in God, fight and do not commit excesses, do not betray or mutilate, and do not kill a child, and when you meet Your enemy is among the polytheists, so invite them to one of the three times - and if they respond to you, then accept from them and desist from them - invite them to Islam, if they answer you to that, then accept from them, desist from them, then invite them to move from their home to the home of the immigrants. And tell them that if they do that, they will have the same rights as the immigrants.

And they are responsible for what is upon them. If they refuse to change from it, then tell them that they will be like the Bedouins of the Muslims, and the judgment of God will apply to them. It applies to the Muslims, and they have no share in the spoils or spoils, unless they struggle with the Muslims. If they refuse, ask them. If they respond, then accept from them and desist from them.”

This hadith was after the revelation of the Jizyah verse, which was only revealed in the year of Tabuk when the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - fought the Christians in the Levant. And the Jews in Yemen.

This ruling is established among the People of the Book by the agreement of the Muslims, as indicated by the Qur’an and the Sunnah, but they disputed over the jizyah: Should it be taken from Other than the People of the Book? This is simple in its context.

chapters.title: The chapter rejecting the Christians’ claim is that the Qur’an is equal among all religions
paragraphs: [Chapter: Refuting the Christians’ claim that the Qur’an equalizes all religions]

They said: And He said in Surat Al-Baqarah: {Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Christians, and the Sabians - whoever believes in God and the Last Day and does righteousness. They will have their reward with their Lord, and there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve” [Al-Baqarah: 62].
So he made this statement equal to all people: Jews, Muslims, and others.

The answer is to say: First: You have no proof in this verse for what you want, for it is equal between you and the Jews and the Sabians. And you and the Muslims agree that the Jews are infidels ever since the Messiah was sent to them and they rejected him.

Likewise, the Sabians, when a messenger was sent to them and they rejected him, are infidels. If the verse contains praise for your religion that you followed after the sending of Muhammad, then it contains praise for the religion of the Jews as well, and this is false in your view and in the opinion of the Jews. Muslims.
If it does not contain praise of the Jews after abrogation and alteration, then it does not contain praise of the Christian religion after abrogation and alteration.
The same can be said of a Jew, if he uses it as evidence of the validity of his religion.

Also, the Christians declare the Jews to be unbelievers, so if their religion is true then the Jews must be declared unbelievers, and if it is false then their religion must be invalidated. From the invalidity of one of the two religions, it is impossible for the verse to praise them, and to be equal between them.

So it was known that she did not praise either of them after abrogating and changing them, but rather the meaning of the verse is that those who believe in Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace -, And those who were Jewish were those who followed Moses - peace be upon him - and they were the ones who followed his law before abrogation and alteration, and the Christians who followed Christ - Peace be upon him -, and they are those who were according to his law before abrogation and alteration.
And the Sabians, and they are the pure-blooded Sabians, like those who were among the Arabs and others who followed the religion of Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac before the change. And abrogation.

The Arabs from the descendants of Ishmael, and others who were neighbors of the ancient house that Abraham and Ishmael had built, were of the same religion. Abraham until some of the governors of Khuza’ah changed his religion, namely Amr bin Luhay, and he was the first to change the religion of Abraham by polytheism and prohibiting what God did not forbid him, and that is why the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw Amr bin Luhay dragging his reed - that is, his intestines - through the fire, and he was the first to He sailed the lake, took away the sediments, and changed the religion of Abraham.”

Likewise, the children of Ishaq, who, before sending Moses, adhered to the religion of Abraham, were among the happy and praised ones. The religion of Moses, Christ, Abraham, and others like them are those whom God Almighty praised: {Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Christians, and the Sabians, are of Whoever believes in God and the Last Day and does righteousness, they will have their reward with their Lord, and there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.} [Al-Baqarah: 62].

The People of the Book, after abrogation and alteration, are not among those who believe in God, nor in the Last Day, and do righteous deeds, as God Almighty said: {Fight those who do not They believe in neither God nor the Last Day, nor do they forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, nor do they follow the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture until they are given The tribute is at hand, while they are humble.} [At-Tawbah: 29].

It was previously mentioned that he declared the People of the Book to be infidels who changed the religion of Moses and Christ, and denied Christ or Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - in anything other than Place, and these are clear verses, and many texts, and this is frequent and known by necessity from the religion of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace.

But these Christians practiced in the Qur’an what they practiced in the Torah and the Gospel. They called the precise, clear, clear texts that do not It has only one meaning, and they cling to what is similar and possible, even if there is something in it that indicates the opposite of what they wanted, as God Almighty said about them. And in their likes:

{It is He who has sent down to you the Book; among it are verses that are decisive, they are the foundation of the Book, and others are allegorical. As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow what He made up similarities in it, seeking to confuse it and seeking to give it an interpretation, but no one knows its interpretation except God, and those who are firmly rooted in knowledge say, “We believe in it.” From our Lord, and none remember except those of understanding.” [Al Imran: 7].

chapters.title: The final answer to their claim is that it is not appropriate for them to abandon the word of God that they have, which the Qur’an has glorified
paragraphs: [Chapter: Refuting their claim that it is not appropriate for them to abandon the Word of God which they have, which the Qur’an has magnified]

They said: Then he praised our offerings and threatened us, if we neglected what was with us and disbelieved in what was revealed to us, that He would punish us with a painful punishment that no one had ever punished. Knowing, by His saying that in Surah Al-Ma’idah: {When the disciples said, “O Jesus, son of Mary, is it possible for your Lord to send down to us a table of Heaven. He said, “Fear Allah if you are believers.” [Al-Ma’idah: 112] (112) “They said, ‘We want to eat from it and our hearts will be at ease, and we will know that you have told us the truth.’” And we will be among its witnesses.} [Al-Ma’idah:

113] (113) {Jesus, son of Mary, said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven that will be a feast for us, for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You. And provide for us, and You are the Best of Providers.} [Al-Ma’idah: 114] (114) {Allah said, “Indeed, I am sending it down to you. But whoever of you disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment that I will never disbelieve.” I will punish him as no one of the worlds” [Al-Ma’idah: 115].
The table is the holy offering that is offered with it in every Mass.

The answer is to say: This is a clear lie about the Qur’an in this place, just as you lied about it in other places, for it is not in The verses do not mention your offerings in any way, but they only mention the table that God Almighty sent down in the era of Christ, peace be upon him. And their saying: The table is the offering that is offered with it in every Mass, is, firstly, a statement for which there is no evidence, and secondly:

It is a well-known statement of corruption due to necessity from the religion of the Muslims who quoted this Qur’an from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, its wording. Its meaning is that they agree that the table is a table that God sent down from heaven during the time of Christ - peace be upon him -, and its story is famous. In general, the books are known to both the general public and the private, and no one said that they are Christian offerings, and there is nothing in the wording of the verse that indicates that, rather It indicates the opposite of that, as the verse makes it clear that the table is sent down from heaven, and their offerings are with them on earth, not sent down from heaven.

In the verse, Jesus said: “O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven that will be a feast for us, for the first of us and the last, and a sign from You, and provide us with And You are the Best of Providers.} [Al-Ma’idah: 114] (114) {Allah said, “Indeed, I am sending it down to you. But whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a punishment that I will not punish anyone else.” Of the worlds} [Al-Maeda: 115].

And at the beginning of the words: {When the disciples said, “O Jesus, son of Mary, is it possible for your Lord to send down to us a table from heaven?” He said, “Fear God.” You are believers.} [Al-Ma’idah: 112] (112) {They said, “We want to eat from it, and our hearts will be at peace, and we will know that you have told us the truth, and we will be witnesses to it.”} [Al-Ma’idah: 113].
Where is this among their offerings available today?

chapters.title: The chapter on Islam honoring Christ, the servant of God and His Messenger
paragraphs: [Chapter: Islam’s honor for Christ, the servant of God and His Messenger]

They said: And when this statement was put forward, because it is not appropriate for people of understanding to neglect the Holy Spirit and the Word of God, to which He bore witness in This Book is full of great things. He said about the Word of God: {And there is not one of the People of the Book who does not believe in it before his death and the Day of Resurrection. He will be a witness over them.} [An-Nisa: 159].
And the answer:

God Almighty did not send Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - by neglecting the rights of Christ - peace be upon him - but rather commanded him to believe. In Christ and what he brought, just as he commanded him to believe in Moses and what he brought, and just as Christ commanded faith in Moses and what he brought, but he He ordered the neglect of whatever religion was invented that God did not legislate on the tongue of Christ - peace be upon him - and what God abrogated from His law on the tongue of Muhammad - May God’s prayers and peace be upon him - he ignores what is changed and what is abrogated, just as God commanded the Messiah to ignore the religion that the Jews invented that did not His law, and what he abrogated from the law of Moses.

Just as the Messiah commanded to ignore what was changed and abrogated from the Torah that Moses - peace be upon him - brought, and this was not a neglect of what It is obligatory by right of the Torah and Moses - peace be upon him -. Likewise, if the religion of the People of the Gospel was neglected if it was changed or abrogated, it would not have been Neglecting what is due from the Gospel and Christ, but rather what Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - brought, includes belief in all the books and the messengers. And that we make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit, as God Almighty said:

{Say, “We believe in God and in what was revealed to us, and what was sent down to Abraham, and Ishmael, and Isaac, and Jacob, and the tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus, and what The prophets have been given from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit.} [Al-Baqarah: 136].

The Christians are like the Jews. They believed in some and disbelieved in others. So what is appropriate among those of understanding is that we believe in all the books of God? And His Messengers, or do we believe in some and disbelieve in part? And what is proper among those of understanding is that we should worship God alone, not associating anything with Him? We worship Him according to what He has legislated on the tongue of His Messenger, or we innovate polytheism and innovated acts of worship unless God has sent down a book for it or sent it. A Messenger and equal to the polytheists who worship idols?

God Almighty said: {And the Jews said, “Uzair is the son of God,” and the Christians said, “The Messiah is the son of God.” That is what they say with their mouths, imitating the words of Those who disbelieved before - God will fight them. How will they be spared? [At-Tawbah: 30].

And He Almighty said: {Say, O People of the Book, come to a word that is common between us and you: that we worship none but Allah, and that we do not associate anything with Him, nor Some of us take others as lords besides God. But if they turn away, then say, “Bear witness that we are Muslims.” [Al Imran: 64].

The Muslims did not neglect the Holy Spirit and the Word of God, and God Almighty said about the Word of God: “And there is not one of the People of the Book who believes.” with it before his death} [An-Nisa: 159].

Rather, they are those who followed his religion and the religion of the messengers before him, for the religion of the prophets - peace be upon them - is all the same, as is proven in the two Sahih books on the authority of the Prophet - May God’s prayers and peace be upon him - he said: We, the prophets, have one religion.

And God Almighty said: {He has prescribed for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah, which We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, that you should establish religion, and do not become divided concerning it.” [Al-Shura: 13].

The religion of all the messengers is one religion, and their laws and approaches are as diverse as the law of one Messenger, so the religion of Christ is the religion of Moses, and it was the religion of Hebron before them, and the religion of Muhammad after them, even though Christ was following the law of the Torah, then God abrogated on his tongue what He abrogated. Among them, before and after abrogation, his religion was the religion of Moses, and he did not neglect the religion of Moses.

Likewise, Muslims follow the religion of Christ, Moses, Abraham, and the rest of the messengers, and they are the ones who followed Christ, and for this reason God made them above the Christians. Until the Day of Resurrection.

The Christians who changed the religion of Christ and denied Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - are innocent of the religion of Christ, and Christ is innocent of them, like the innocence of Moses. From those who changed and changed their religion and denied Christ.

Muslims are more in their reverence of Christ - peace be upon him - and in following him in truth than the Christians who changed their religion and went against it. They believe him in everything he tells about himself, and they do not distort what he says about its context, and they do not interpret his words other than what he intends, and the words of others. The prophets, as the Christians did, for they quoted from Christ that he said, baptize people in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, and this then What Christ said, it is explained by his language and his habit in his speech and the habit of all the prophets, (and not in the words of Christ nor in the words of other The Prophets, nor the words of others, that the Word of God) which exists in Himself, Glory be to Him and - the Most High - is called the Son, nor is the Holy Spirit, nor is His ancient attribute called A Son, nor a Holy Spirit, and the name of the Son is never found in the words of the prophets except to a created being.

What is meant in that language is that he is a chosen one beloved of God, as they say that he said to Israel: (You are my son, my firstborn), and to David (You are my son and my beloved), and that Christ said to the disciples (my father and your father), making him the father of all, and they are all created, so the name The Son is related to Christ, who is created humanity. So these people deliberately misled and made the name of the Son related to the Godhead, ancient, eternal, begotten. Uncreated.

They claimed that what is meant by “son” is the Son by birth, and He is the created being, and He is the Son by nature, and He is the Ancient, Eternal, and Unbegotten. The created being, and this distinction they created and invented, and it is never found in the words of Christ or anyone else that he called the Ancient and Eternal One a son, nor made He has an ancient son, begotten and not created, and he never called any of God’s attributes a son.
Likewise, the word “Holy Spirit” is found in more than one place in the words of the prophets - peace be upon them - by this it does not mean at all the life of God or any attribute. A list of it.

What is meant by it is what God supported the prophets and saints with, and placed in their hearts of His guidance, light, revelation, and support. Among the things that are sent down by the angels, and this which the prophets call the Holy Spirit, Christ was not specific to it, according to the agreement of Muslims and the people of The Book. Rather, He revealed it to other prophets and righteous people as it is found in their books: Indeed, the Holy Spirit was in David. And others, and it was also among the disciples among them.
Thus, the Seal of the Messengers used to say to Hassan bin Thabit: “The Holy Spirit is with you as long as you defend his Prophet,” and he said, “Oh God, support him.” “By the Holy Spirit.”
