And if they say: He meant Christian humanity by that, then there is no difference between that humanity and all other humanity, even though what is meant by that text is Adam, the father of humanity. By agreement of the nations, humanity itself is not the Word and Spirit of God.

Fifth: If it were assumed that what was meant by this is that the word of God resembles itself in some ways, such as the fact that it is as ancient as Him - then it would not This indicates the three hypostases.

Likewise, the well-known expression is: (We will create human beings in our image, our likeness.) This does not indicate the Trinity in any way. The resemblance of a thing to another is due to its resemblance to it in some ways, and that does not require similarity, which requires that they share in what it is necessary to do. It is permissible and not, and when it is said: This is the Living, the Knowing, the Powerful, and this is the Living, the Knowing, the Powerful, then they are similar in the designation of the Living, the Knowing, and the Powerful - no. This requires that this term be similar to this term in what is obligatory, permissible, and prohibited.

Rather, here are three things: One of them: the common destiny, in which they are similar, and it is a comprehensive meaning that is not specific to either of them, and there is no Completely, generally, and in common, except within the knowledge of the scholar.
The second: What is specific to him, just as the Lord is specific to what He does of life, knowledge, and power.

The third: What is specific to (that person, just as it is specific to him) the servant, such as life, knowledge, and ability, so what the Lord Almighty and Majestic has specified for him is not The servant shares it with him, and none of the shortcomings that are permissible for the servant’s characteristics are permissible for him. The Lord does not share with him what is specific to the servant, nor does He deserves some of the perfect qualities that are unique to the Lord Almighty.

As for the common destiny, such as the universal meaning fixed in the mind of man, this does not necessitate the characteristics of the Creator nor the characteristics of the creature. Participation in it is not prohibited.

And the word of the Torah in it: (We will create a human being in our image, resembling us). He did not say: in our likeness, and it is like what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in the hadith. The correct one is (Let none of you say: May God disgrace your face and the face of one who resembles your face, for God Almighty created Adam in His image) and he did not mention The prophets, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them, such as Moses and Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him - except for the word “similar” without the word “like.”

People have disputed over whether the word semblance or proverb has one meaning or two meanings, based on two opinions: one of them is that they have one meaning, and that What is indicated by the word proverb, both absolute and specific, is indicated by the word similarity, and this is the opinion of a group of theorists.

The second: Its meaning in general is different in language, law, and reason, even if with the restriction and the context, what is intended is meant by one of them. In the end, and this is what most people say, and this difference is based on a rational issue, which is that is it permissible for something to resemble A thing is from one way to another, and the people have two opinions regarding that: So whoever is prevented from resembling it from one way to another, he said: likeness and resemblance. One, and whoever says: A thing may resemble another thing in one way but not another - makes a distinction between them in general terms.

This is what the majority of people say, for the mind knows that symptoms such as colors are suspected of being colours, even though black is not Such as whiteness. Similarly, bodies and essences, according to the majority of rational people, are similar in terms of the term “body” and “essence,” even if they are Their realities are not identical. The reality of water is not similar to the reality of earth, nor is the reality of plants similar to the reality of animals, nor is the reality of fire similar. Similar to the reality of water, even though they share in that each of them is an essence, a body, and exists on its own.
Also, it is known in the language that it is said: This is similar to this, and it has a resemblance to this, since it is similar to it in some ways, even if it is Contrary to him in reality.
God Almighty said: {And bring him resembling him} [Al-Baqarah: 25].

And he said: {Among them are clear verses that are the mother of the Book, and others are allegorical. As for those in whose hearts there is deviation, they follow what is ambiguous therein, seeking temptation and seeking an interpretation for it} [Al Imran: 7].
{And those who do not know say, “If only God would not speak to us or a sign would come to us.” Those before them said, “Their saying is similar.” Their hearts} [Al-Baqarah: 118].

He described the two sayings with similarity, and the hearts with similarity, not with similarity. Even if hearts share this statement, they are different, not similar. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The lawful is clear and the forbidden is clear.” Clearly, and between that there are similar matters that many people do not know.”
This indicates that some people know them, and in the same way, they are not the same, but some of them are forbidden and some of them are permissible.

The sixth aspect: His saying: (We will create a creation in our likeness) does not address His description, such as His words and His life based on it, for that He is not a creature, and then this does not address the divinity that they claim was shielded by humanity, for theology is not a creature.

As for the human being, it is like all other human beings, and it has no specificity to it, to be similar to God without all other human beings, so His saying: Who is He? What is the likeness of a created being other than His word and spirit? -False in every respect.

As for his saying: (Behold, Adam has become like one of us), and their saying: This is a clear statement that God said this saying to his son, Spirit. He sanctified him. If they wanted to make him who became like one of us his son, this would be futile. If what is meant by this son is the word that is an attribute of God, then nothing was created for her to become like one of them, and nothing was created for her to become like one of them. She is called Adam, but God did not call her son.

And if what is meant by him is the humanity of Christ, then that is an innovative creature who refrains from being like the ancient and eternal one. Also, God said about Adam, and Adam He is not the Messiah, and it is not permissible to say: Adam, meaning the Messiah, just as it is not permissible to say: Adam disobeyed, meaning the Messiah. He said: (Behold, Adam has become like one of us.) This is a reference to something that happened in the past time, it is not a reference to what will happen after that. For thousands of years, and if they meant that God said to His Son, who is His Word and His Spirit, and this is what they mean, as they say:

He said this saying mocking Adam, meaning that he asked to become like one of us. He thus became naked and exposed, and would be They doubted his saying: (from us) because it was expressed in the plural form, (and also if they meant this by saying (we create human beings in our image And it is similar to us.) So they protested against the trinity in the plural form.

This is what the Christians of Najran used as evidence against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. They invoked God Almighty’s words (Indeed), (We) and they said: This indicates Although they were three, and this was one of the similarities which they followed, seeking temptation and seeking its interpretation, and they left the decisive and clear one who It can only bear one, for God has made clear in all His divine books that He is one God, and that He has no partner, nor is He like Him.

And His saying: (Indeed), (We) is a word that applies in all languages to one who has partners and examples, and to the One who is greatly obeyed. Helpers who obey him, even if they are not partners or equals, and God Almighty created everything other than Him, so it is impossible for Him to have a partner or an equal. And the angels and the rest of the worlds are His soldiers, the Almighty.
The Almighty said: {And none know the hosts of your Lord except Him} [Al-Muddaththir: 31].
And the Almighty said: {And to Allah belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Mighty, Wise} [Al-Fath: 7].

So if one of the kings says: We, and we, and they do not mean that they are three kings, then the Owner of the kingdom is the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of everything. And His Sovereign is more deserving of saying: We, and we, even though He has no partner or equal. Rather, His are the hosts of the heavens and the earth.

Also, it is known that Adam did not ask to become like God or like His attributes such as His knowledge and life, and also it is not in the apparent meaning of the wording. God addressed His attributes with that.

Also, the attribute that refers to the one being described does not address or be addressed, but rather addresses the one being described, and Adam had not created the humanity of Christ, nor other human beings until he addresses him, so he knew that their claim that God addressed his attributes, which they called the Son and the Holy Spirit - is false talk. Rather, he may address His angels.

And Adam, peace be upon him, wanted what Satan coveted of immortality and dominion, as God Almighty said: {Then Satan whispered to him, saying, “O Adam, do you I will direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not fade away.” [Taha: 120].

chapters.title: A chapter on the refutation of their reasoning regarding what was stated in the command to destroy the people of Lot based on the lordship of the son
paragraphs: [Chapter: Refuting their evidence based on what was stated in the command to destroy the people of Lot on the basis of the son’s mastery]

They said: And God said, when He destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, He said in the Torah: (And the Lord rained fire from the Lord from the sky upon Sodom and Gomorrah. And as a sulphur, he thus explained the lordship of the Father and the Son.

The answer is: Their argument for this is the utmost falsehood for reasons: one of which is: calling God, his knowledge and his life, as Son and Lord. False naming. In the Torah, Moses did not name any of the attributes of God by the name of the Son or by the name of the Father. The plaintiff’s claim is that Moses, peace be upon him, wanted That the Lord has any of the attributes of God, or that He has an attribute called His Son - is false talk.

The second: If it were determined that the attribute of God is named thus, then it is known that the one who rained is the one with whom it rained, and the rain did not occur at One of them (and the other is rain, just as it is not permissible to say that one of them was created) from something in the presence of the other, and neither of them sent down rain from a cloud. The other.

Third: The attribute does not do anything, nor does it have anything. Rather, it is dependent on what is described, and the essence characterized by the attribute is the one that does it. And then what will happen will happen.

Fourth: This is in the same position as his saying: (The Lord rained from Himself), but He placed the apparent noun in the place of the implicit word to make it clear, because the matter belongs to Him. Alone in this and that.
An example of this is in the Qur’an, as it says: {Al-Haqqah - what is Al-Haqqah} [Al-Haqqah: 1-2].
{Al-Qari’ah - What is Al-Qari’ah?} [Al-Qari’ah: 1-2].
And the Almighty said: {The revelation of the Book from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing} [Ghafir: 2].
{A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful} [Fussilat: 2].
By God, it is He who sends down, and He did not say from me.

chapters.title: A chapter refuting their reasoning from what was reported from David regarding the Lordship of Christ
paragraphs: [Chapter: A response to their evidence based on what was reported from David regarding the lordship of Christ]
They said: We mention a third, and David said in the Psalms in the one hundred and nineth Psalm, saying: (The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies Under your feet.)

The answer is in a number of ways: One of them is that it is not permissible to mean by (my Lord) any of the attributes of God, for He did not name David or any of The prophets are nothing of the attributes of God as Lord or Son, and no one said to any of the attributes of God: O Lord, have mercy on me, nor did he say to the knowledge of God or His word. Or His power: O Lord, and if they do not call the attributes of God Lord, and if Christ were one of His attributes, it is not possible for that to be what is meant. In the word of the Lord, how can it be that His humanity is so far removed from divinity that it is meant by that?
It was known that they did not mean by that either divinity or humanity.

The second: That he said: The Lord said to my Lord, so he added the second to it without the first, and that it is his Lord who created him, and in general what the Christians have of The exaggeration is that they say: A true God from a true God, and they make him the creator, but they make him more worthy than the father in that he is the Lord of David. This is what they did not say, and it is an apparent falsehood.

Third: This does not mention the three hypostases. Its purpose, if it were as they interpreted it, was to mention the Son. As for the hypostases Of the three, none of the Books of God that are in their hands, let alone the Qur’an, was spoken of, neither with its wording nor its meaning, but rather they invented a word. The hypostasis, and they expressed by it what they made the meaning of the books of God, while they do not indicate that, so in that they were translators of the words of God, and they did not They understand its meaning, but they do not express it with a phrase that indicates what is intended.
Fourth: He said: To my Lord, and this is what is meant by the Master, as Joseph said: {Indeed, my Lord is the best of my abode} [Joseph: 23].
And he said to the king’s servant: “Remember me before your Lord” [Joseph: 42].
And God Almighty said: {Then Satan made him forget the remembrance of his Lord} [Joseph: 42].

For this reason, the first was mentioned in general terms and the second was mentioned in a specific manner, so the meaning is: And God said to my master: The Lord of the worlds said to my master, and he called him a master out of humility. David and glorified him, because he believed that he was better than him.

chapters.title: A chapter on his saying in the Torah, who said to me, “You are my son, and today I have begotten you.”
paragraphs: [Chapter: His saying in the Torah who said to me, ‘You are my son, and today I have begotten you.’”
They said: We mention a fourth, and he said in the second psalm: (He who said to me: You are my son, and today I have begotten you).

The answer is in a number of ways: One of them is that this does not include naming the attributes of God - His knowledge and His life - as a Son, nor does it mention the three hypostases. There is no proof in it for anything you claim.

The second: This is an argument against them, because he named his son David, so he knew that the son’s name was not specific to Christ, peace be upon him, but rather he named He changed another of his servants as a son, so he knew that the name of the son is not a name for his attributes, but rather it is a name for the one of his slaves who raised him.

In that case, the Messiah would not be called a son because the Lord or his attribute was united with him, but rather as he called David a son, and as he called Israel. A son, and he said: (You are my firstborn son).

This is in their books, as mentioned, (So if what is in their books is the word of God, then there is no argument in it, because He intended the educator, and if it is not the word God and His Messengers) so there is no evidence for it, because saying something other than infallible is not evidence.

Third: That his saying: (Today I have begotten you) indicates the occurrence of this action, and with them the word that they call the Son is born from The Father is ancient and everlasting, as they said in their faithfulness (and in one Lord, Jesus Christ, the only Son of God, who was born of the Father before all ages Light from Light, true God from true God, of the essence of his Father, begotten, not created, of one essence with the Father, by whom all things were made.

According to them, this Son was born of the Father before all ages, and that was born on the day He spoke to him after the creation of David, but he was not on this day. What is new is evidence of the existence of that ancient thing.

The fourth aspect: If the father in their language is the Lord who raises his servant, greater than the father raises his son, then the meaning of the word Giving birth is something that fits the meaning of this fatherhood, so the meaning is: Today I have made you a chosen chosen one.

Christians may make the speech, which is a pronoun for other than Christ, mean Christ. They may say: What is meant by this Messiah, and this It is falsehood and the word does not indicate it, and as true as it is, it indicates that Christ is the created humanity, and He is called the Son, for His saying (And today I have given birth to you.)

And divinity, according to them, was born before the ages, and then, if what is meant by it is the day of his birth, then the meaning is: I created you, even if it was the day They chose him, so what is meant is “today I have chosen you and loved you,” as if he said: “today I have made you a son and a son,” according to their language.

chapters.title: A chapter on the refutation of their reasoning regarding what was mentioned in the Torah regarding the words of God to Moses and what that benefits from the multiplicity of His divinity, Glory be to Him.
paragraphs: [Chapter: A response to their reasoning based on what was mentioned in the Torah from the words of God to Moses and what that benefits him in terms of the multiplicity of his divinity, Glory be to Him]

They said: We mention a fifth, and in the second book of the Torah: And God spoke to Moses from the bush, saying: (I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob), and he did not say, “I am the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Rather, he repeated the name of God three times, saying: “I am a God and a God.” To achieve the issue of the three hypostases in his theology.

The answer is: Invoking this as evidence against the three hypostases is one of the most corrupt things, and this appears from several reasons: one of which is that if I mean, with the word of God, I hypostasize existence, and with God’s word a second time, I hypostasize the Word, and with the third, I hypostasize life, it would have been The one hypostasis is the God of Abraham, the second hypostasis is the God of Isaac, and the third hypostasis is the God of Jacob, so each of the hypostases is The three are the god of one of the three prophets, and the two hypostases are not his gods.

This is blasphemy among them, and among all people of that religion. Also, it is necessary from that that the gods be three, and they say: God. One, then when they say: Each of the hypostases is one God, then they make everyone the God of every prophet, so if they use this text as evidence They say that the god of every prophet must not be the god of the other prophet, even though the gods are three.

The second aspect: It is said: Indeed, God is Lord of the worlds, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, Lord of the throne, and Lord of all things. Is it necessary that He be Lord? He is not the Lord of the heavens, the Lord of the earth, the Lord of everything.

Likewise it is said: The God of Moses and the God of Muhammad, while we say: The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, (Are there five gods? And Jacob said To his sons: (What will you worship after me?) They said: We worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac.
Did you think that he established two gods: one of them was his god, and the other was the god of the three? !
The third aspect: The conjunction is sometimes to contrast essences, and sometimes to contrast attributes, as the Almighty says: {Glorify the name of your Lord Most High} [Al-A’la: 1] (1).
And He who created is the One who destined and brought forth, and likewise His saying: {Your God and the God of your fathers} [Al-Baqarah: 133].

And He is the One, Glory be to Him. And Ibrahim Al-Khalil, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said to his people: {He said, “Have you seen what you used to worship?” [Al-Shu’ara’: 75] (75) {You and your forefathers are the most ancient} [Al-Shu’ara’: 76] (76) {For they are my enemy except the Lord of the worlds} [Al-Shu’ara’: 77] (77) {It is He who created me, and it is He who guides me} [Al-Shu’ara’: 78] (78) {And it is He who feeds me and gives me drink} [Al-Shu’ara’: 79] (79) {And when I am sick, it is He who heals me} [Al-Shu’ara’: 80] (80) {And He who causes me to die, then He will revive} [Al-Shu'ara': 81] (81) {And it is He who I hope will forgive me my sins on the Day of Judgment} [Al-Shu'ara': 82]
And He who created it is the one who feeds it and gives it drink, and it is He who causes it to die and then brings it back to life.

His saying in the Torah: The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, is from this section, and this is not specific to three, rather it is said in The two, the four, and the five, according to what the speaker intends to mention of the attributes, and in this there is an benefit that is not found in his saying: God. Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. If that was said, it would only mean that he was worshiped by the three. It does not indicate that they worshiped him independently, each one of them. Some of them worshiped Him in a way that was specific to Him, but it was not the same as the worship of the first.

Also, when it is said: The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, it indicates the necessary worship of each of them, and when it is said: And a god, it indicates He is worshiped by each of the three, so he brought him back in the name of the God who clearly indicates worship through the word that includes it, and in that is the appearance The meaning for the listener and its ramifications into an image for him without thought - something that is not in the meaning of the binding.

chapters.title: A chapter refuting their reasoning based on Isaiah’s testimony regarding the fulfillment of the Trinity
paragraphs: [Chapter: A response to their argument based on Isaiah’s testimony to the fulfillment of the Trinity]
They said: Likewise, (Isaiah) testified to the fulfillment of the Trinity through the oneness of its essence, and that is when He said: (Lord of hosts), and by His saying:

(Lord of the heavens and the earth) There are many such sayings in the Torah and the Psalms. Even the Jews acknowledge these prophecies, but they do not know It has an interpretation, and they acknowledge that, and do not deny a single word of it, but their hearts are closed off from understanding it because of its hardness towards What we mentioned before that, and that when they gathered in their church every Saturday, the accusers would stand before them, and say these Hebrew words: Its interpretation, and they do not deny it, (We sanctify you, we venerate you, and we give you a three-fold sanctification as it is written on the tongue of your Prophet).
Then they all shouted in response: (Holy, holy, holy, Lord of hosts and Lord of the heavens and the earth).

How clear is their acknowledgment of the Trinity, and how strong is their disbelief in its meaning, we are in favor of this clear statement that God said in the Torah. And in the books of the prophets they made Him into three persons, one essence, one nature, one God, one Lord, one Creator, and He is the One We say: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

The answer: As for what is in the books of the prophets, peace be upon them, regarding the duplication of the name of the Lord when it is added to another creature, it is of the type Deuteronomy of the name of God,
This does not necessitate the multiplicity of lords and gods, and this is why it does not necessitate making them two or four if the word is mentioned twice. And four.

Likewise, if it is mentioned three times, it does not mean that there are three lords, and they also do not say that there are three lords and three gods. If it were This indicates three lords and three gods. It indicates the opposite of what they said. Rather, they claim that they only affirm one God. But they contradict each other and claim that there are three gods, and they say that they are one god.

The books do not indicate their contradictory statement in any way. As for what they mentioned about the Jews’ recognition of the words of these prophecies, They claimed that they did not know an interpretation for it, so if by interpretation they meant its interpretation and what its word indicates, then this is apparent and not hidden. On boys, Jews and others.

But the Christians claimed something that the word does not indicate, and if they intended by interpretation a meaning that contradicted the apparent meaning of the word, then this is only needed if Its apparent meaning was false, and it is not permissible to mean it, and it is not what they mentioned here in this regard, but rather the divine books, in which there are many examples, such as: This is what the People of the Book and the Muslims say, and three lords or three gods do not understand it except he who follows his desires without Guidance from God, and he said a different word, which will be pardoned by whoever misunderstands it, and something like this is found in all speech, it is said:
This is the Emir of such-and-such a country, and the Emir of such-and-such a country, and the Emir of such-and-such a country, and he is one prince.
It is said: This is the Messenger of God to the unlettered, and a Messenger to the People of the Book, and a Messenger to the jinn and mankind, and he is one Messenger.

chapters.title: A chapter refuting what was stated in the Torah regarding the saying: We sanctify you, we venerate you, and we give you a three-fold sanctification, just as it was written on the tongue of your prophet Isaiah.
paragraphs: [Chapter: A response to what was stated in the Torah, which says, “We sanctify you, we venerate you, and we give you a three-fold sanctification, as is written by your prophet Isaiah.”]
As for their saying: (We sanctify you, we venerate you, and we give you a threefold sanctification, as it is written on the tongue of your prophet Isaiah).

And their saying: Holy, holy, holy, Lord of hosts and Lord of the heavens and the earth), so it is said: This statement is clear in that the triangle is the same Sanctification is not the same sanctifying God.

And so is their saying: (Holy, holy, holy). They sanctified him three times, for he said: (We sanctify you, and we sanctify you three times.) So he put the three-part accusative on the noun that is accusative by the verb of sanctification, and said: We sanctify you with a threefold sanctification.

(So the accusative case of sanctification is on the noun), as you say: I glorified you with a triple glorification, meaning I glorified you three times, and He said: We glorify you three times, meaning we glorify you three times in sanctification. For you, he did not say: You are three, but rather they made themselves the ones who sanctify the threefold sanctification, and they are triangulating for it, and this is clear in that they They glorify Him three times, but they do not glorify three gods or three hypostases.

This is as it is in the Sunan on the authority of Ibn Masoud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “(If the servant says while bowing: Glory be to my Lord The Great, three times, then he has completed his bowing, and that is below, and if he says in his prostration: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, three times, then his prostration has been completed, and that "Below", and praise is the sanctification of the Lord, and the lowest is to sanctify Him three times, so it means: Sanctify Him three times, do not limit yourself to once. One.

And for this reason they say in response: Holy, holy, holy, so they sanctify Him three times. It is known that what is meant is a triple sanctification as indicated by it. Its wording, and what they do in compliance with this command, and what is done in return for that, such as tripling its sanctification, and that it be sanctified three times without For the sanctuary to be three persons, this is something that no prophet of the prophets ever spoke of, either verbally or in meaning, but rather all the prophets. Peace be upon them. They established one God to whom are the most beautiful names.

Its names are multiple, indicating its multiple attributes, and this is not limited to three names, or three attributes, (and attributes are not a hypostasis that is An entity and an attribute, but there is only one entity that has multiple attributes, so the multiplicity of attributes is not in the entity that they call essence, nor in the entity. And the characteristic they call the hypostasis.

chapters.title: A chapter refuting their affirmation of the Jews’ acknowledgment of the Trinity and their disbelief in its meaning
paragraphs: [Chapter: Refuting their affirmation of the Jews’ acknowledgment of the Trinity and their disbelief in its meaning]
They said: How great is their acknowledgment of the Trinity, and how strong is their disbelief in its meaning.

It is said: This is an apparent slander against the Jews, and if the Jews were infidels, their disbelief was not for the sake of denying the Trinity. If they acknowledged it, it would have increased their disbelief and increased their torment.

Just as when the Christians disbelieved, their disbelief was not due to their acknowledgment that the Messiah who had been preached about and who had appeared was not the Antichrist who The Jews are waiting for him, and when he comes out, they are his followers, and the Muslims are killing them with the worst of murderers, to the point that trees and stones say: O Muslim There is a Jew behind me. Come and kill him.
Rather, if they disbelieved in Christ as the Jews disbelieved, that would be an increase in their disbelief.

And among the Jews, and among them, in the Torah, there is pure monotheism that nullifies your triangulation, something that is not hidden except from those who turn away from the remembrance of God. He who sent it down, and the guidance with which He guided His servants.

chapters.title: The chapter on their return once again to adherence to the Trinity due to what they had previously transmitted and referred to from the words of the prophets
paragraphs: [Chapter: Their return once again to adherence to the Trinity due to what they had previously transmitted and referred to from the words of the prophets]
They said: For the sake of this clear statement that God made in the Torah, and in the books of the prophets, We make three hypostases: one essence, One God, one Creator.
He is what we say: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

The answer is from several aspects: One of them: that in the Torah and the divine books there is proof of the unity of God, denying the multiplicity of gods, and denying There is no mention of the hypostases, either verbally or in meaning, as They make the hypostasis a name for the essence with the attribute, and the essence is one, and the multiplicity is in the attributes, not in the essence.

It is not possible for one attribute to be united without the other, nor without the essence, so it is impossible for a hypostasis to be united or dissolved into any of the creatures without The other hypostasis, and there is no confirmation of three hypostases or three attributes to the exclusion of anything else in any of the divine books, nor the words of the disciples. There is no proof of a true God from a true God, nor naming the attributes of God - such as His words and His life - as a Son, nor a God, nor a Lord, nor is there a proof The union of the Lord, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, with any of the human beings, and there are no solutions of one attribute without an entity with other attributes, and even no solutions of the same attribute. What is based on him is in something else, not his knowledge, his speech, his life, or anything else.

Rather, all that they have proven regarding the Trinity, solutions, and unity is not in the books of the prophets that are in their hands, but rather there are sayings in them. Many are clear in contrast to the Qur’an and reason, as they are contrary to reason and the revealed books of God.

Second: They say: We only establish one God, and then they say in their trustworthiness, evidence, and other than that of their words, what is clear By confirming three gods, they contradict each other’s statements and say contradictory statements that are known to be false. A sane person imagined it.

This is not a consistent statement of theirs, as some of the wisest people say: The Christians do not have a statement that a rational person can understand, and no Their sayings are derived from the prophets, so there is neither hearing nor reason with them, as God Almighty said about the inmates of the Fire: {If only we had listened. Or will we understand that we were among the companions of the Blazing Fire?} [Al-Mulk: 10].

They also conceal things contrary to what they reveal, and the majority of people understand their articles contrary to what some of them claim is what they mean, for it may He mentioned above their reasoning for the Torah, and his saying: (And God spoke to Moses from the bush, saying: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob) They said: He did not say: I am the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, but rather he repeated the name of a god three times, saying: I am the God of 00 and his God 00 and his God 00 In order to verify the issue of the Three Persons in His divinity, it is said to them:

And if this repetition only requires proving one God, then you have no argument for it, just as if he said, “I am the God of Abraham and Isaac.” And Jacob, even if it requires affirming three gods: You have affirmed three gods, and you say: We affirm only one god. If the meaning is: He is one God, described as the worshiper of Abraham, the worshiper of Isaac, and the worshiper of Jacob, then you have no argument against him. The Trinity and the Hypostases (such that you make the Hypostasis a name for the essence with an attribute, while the essence is one, so the pluralism in

Attributes are not in the essence, and it is not possible for one attribute to be united without another, nor without the essence, so it is impossible to unite a hypostasis and its substitution with any of the created things. Without the other hypostasis.

The third aspect: Their saying: which is what we say: Father, Son, and the Holy Spirit. It was previously mentioned that this saying they acknowledge that they They did not say it in the beginning, nor did they know of the triune mind which they said in their trustworthiness, then they expressed it with this phrase, but rather this The phrase was transmitted to them in some of the Gospels:

That Christ, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded that people be baptized with it, and in that case, it is necessary, if Christ said it, to see what he meant by it. All of his words and their meanings are examined, and his words are interpreted, in the language in which he spoke, in an interpretation that suits the rest of his words.

These people attributed the words of Christ and the prophets, peace be upon them, to something that their words do not indicate, but rather indicate its opposite, so they called it the word of God or His knowledge, wisdom, or pronunciation - Son, and this is a name they invented. None of the prophets named any of the attributes of God by the name of the Son. Neither in the name of the Lord, nor in the name of God. Then when they introduced this designation, they said: What is meant by Christ by the Son is the Word, and this is a slander. On Christ, peace be upon him, and his words carry a meaning that his words do not indicate.

According to them, the term “son” in their books means one whom God, Blessed and Most High, raised. However, in the words of the prophets, the term “son” is not used with them in the words of the prophets. Never, except for a newly created creature, and it is only applied to humanity and not divinity, so Israel is called the son of Israel and David the son of God, and the disciples Likewise, in fact, in the Gospel of John, in the mention of Christ to his own, that is, his own did not receive him, but to those who did receive him he gave them to be Sons of God, who is neither of blood nor of flesh, nor of man, but of God.

This is news that they are all sons of God, and they acknowledge that there is no divinity in them united with humanity, but rather each of them Pure humanity, so he knew that the Scriptures speak that the word “Son of God” refers to humanity only, and not with them the word “Son of God,” and what is meant by it is a description. One of the attributes of God.

Their saying: By the word “Son,” Christ meant divinity is a clear lie against him, and Christ is not called a son in this sense, and the Holy Spirit did not express it. One of the prophets has it about the life of God, which is His attribute. Rather, the Holy Spirit in the books of God means kingship and guidance. And revelation and support. It is said: the spirit of God, just as it is said: the light of God, the guidance of God, the revelation of God, the kingdom of God, and the Messenger of God. None of the The prophets, by saying: the Spirit of God, and the Holy Spirit - what man means when he says: (my spirit).

Man is composed of a soul and a body, and in his body is a vapor that comes out of the heart and circulates through his body, and he has a cavity from which air emerges. And it enters into it, so when it is said: the human soul, what is meant by it may be the soul that contains the pleasant vapor that is in the body, or it may be meant by it the fragrance that It comes out of the body and enters it.

And God, Blessed and Most High, according to the consensus of Muslims, Jews and Christians, is not the same in spirit and body as a human being, and He, Glory be to Him, is one who has steadfast. It has a cavity, and nothing enters it, and nothing comes out of it, neither vapor nor oscillating air.

Some people may express life with the word “soul,” and God Almighty is living and has life, but the prophets, peace be upon them, did not express it. When they said: The Holy Spirit - the life of God. Rather, they meant by it what God places in the hearts of the prophets and supports them with it, as is meant by the light of God. That, God Almighty said:

{Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth. The likeness of His light is like a niche in which is a lamp. The lamp is in a glass. The glass is as if it were a shining star lit from A blessed tree, an olive tree neither of the East nor of the West, whose oil would almost shine even if no fire touched it. Light upon light. God guides to His light whomsoever He wills. And God sets forth parables for the people, and God is All-Knowing of all things” [An-Nour: 35].

So God set an example of the believer who made his chest like a niche, and his heart like a bottle in the niche, and the light of faith that is in his heart - and he The light of God - is like the light bulb in the bottle, and that light that is in his heart is not the same attribute of God that resides in it.

So it became clear that whenever the knowledgeable person contemplated what the prophets said, and what the heretics of the Christians and others said, he did not find any words for them. The prophets except what indicates the opposite of their misguidance, not what indicates their misguidance.

chapters.title: A chapter refuting their claim that they are not obligated to worship three gods and that they are not to blame for the Trinity based on the testimonies of the prophets that preceded them.
paragraphs: [Chapter: A refutation of their claim that they are not obligated to worship three gods and that they are not to be blamed for the Trinity due to the testimonies they have previously received. the prophets]

They said: We know that it does not oblige us if we say this to worship three gods, but rather one God, just as it does not oblige us if we say: Man, his speech, and his spirit are three human beings, but one human being. And when we say: The flame of fire, the light of fire, and the heat of fire are three fires, nor If we say:

The disk of the sun, the light of the sun, and the rays of the sun are three suns, and if this is our opinion of God, His names are sanctified, and His benefits are majestic, then there is no Blame is upon us, and we are not at fault, since we have not neglected what we have received, nor rejected what we have imitated, and followed anything else, (especially since we have these The clear testimonies and clear evidence from the book that this man brought.

The answer is in a number of ways: one of them is that you declared the multiplicity of gods and lords in the doctrine of your faith, in your reasoning, and other such matters. Your words, this is not something that people have forced you to do, but rather you declare that, as mentioned above:

We believe in one God, Father, Ruler of all, Creator of what is seen and unseen, and in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only Son of God, born of The Father before all ages, Light from the Light of the true God from the true God, of the essence of His Father was born, not created, equal in essence with the Father, and in spirit The Holy Lord, the Giver of Life, who proceeds from the Father, who is with the Father, is worshiped and glorified.

This is a declaration of three lords, and that the Son is a true God from a true God, in addition to your declaration of three lords and your declaration that This is a true god from a true god. You say: This is one God, and this is a statement of the multiplicity of gods while saying of one God.

If you had not mentioned what implies that it is another essence, your words could be interpreted as a conjunction of the adjective, but your words would be greater in disbelief. So you have made Christ the same God the Father, the Creator of what is seen and what is unseen, and this is greater than your disbelief, although this The truth of your words is that you say: Christ is God, and you say:

He is the Son of God (just as God mentioned the two sayings about you in His speech, and declared you to be unbelievers by that, and this is not the saying of a sect and this is the saying of a sect) As some people say, in fact both sayings are said by Christian sects such as the Nestorianism, the Jacobites, the Melkites, and the like, and this is also From your contradiction, if He is God, then He is not the Son of God, whether the attribute is expressed by the Son or some other attribute, for the Father is the Essence. The essence is not the attribute, and if what is meant by the son is the essence with the attribute of speech, as you interpret the hypostasis in that - then this essence is characterized by that. With life, and speech - whether they mean by it knowledge or clarification with knowledge - is with life, connected to the Father, and the adjective is not the same as what is described. Rather, it is not expressed as the son of the narrator, and none of the prophets, peace be upon them, expressed that.

What is meant is that when they said: And in one Lord Jesus Christ - they did not mean to connect the adjective, and that this is the Father as He said: God Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob - this is one God, and the conjunction is due to the difference in the description. If what was meant by the son was the same as the father, it would be This is contrary to their doctrine, and they may have made him a god in and of himself, so they said: two gods, but three, and he is one.

If they had wanted this, it would have been greater in disbelief. Rather, they would have said: And in one Lord, Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, begotten of the Father. All ages, Light from Light, true God from true God, from the essence of His Father, begotten, not created. So they declared that He is Lord, and that He is a true God from a true God, and they declared a second God alongside the first God.
They said, however, that He was begotten of the Father before all ages, and that He was begotten, not created. So they refrained from meaning by that humanity, for Humanity is a created being.

And they say: The Word is born of the Father. The word is an attribute of the speaker and is related to him, and the words are neither about a Lord nor a god, but rather they are the words of the Lord God, just as the rest of the words of God are like the Torah. The Gospel and the Qur’an are not the Lord and God. Then you said: He is equal to the Father in essence. This necessitated that the child be the one who is The Word is essence, and He is equal to the Father in essence, and what is equal is not equal.

This requires proving a second essence equal to the first essence, and it is clear by proving two gods, and they say with that: He is a god. One is one essence, and essence is not said with the knowledge that they express by hypostasis, equal to the essence, which is the essence; For the essence is the essence, and there are not two essences here, one of them is abstract from knowledge, and the other is characterized by it, to the point that it is said: one of them is equal. to the other. Rather, the Lord Almighty is the entity characterized by knowledge. If the father is the abstract entity, then the son is more perfect than the father, and he is The self is with knowledge, and the father is with the son.

They also require that the Son be some part of the Holy Spirit; For in their faithfulness they made the Holy Spirit the Lord who gives life, and the Lord who gives life is the entity characterized by life, and the abstract entity is some That is, if the Father is the abstract entity, then the Son is a part of the Holy Spirit.

Then you said about the hypostasis of the Holy Spirit, whom you made the Lord and Giver of life: He proceeds from the Father, worshiped and glorified, speaking through the prophets. If the one who emanates is a living Lord, then this is proof of a third God, and you have made the living entity emanating from the abstract entity, and in each of them there is There is no secret of disbelief and contradiction.

Then you made this third prostrate to Him, and the one prostrated to Him is the worshiped God, and this is a statement of prostration to a third god along with what There is a contradiction in it, then you made him a spokesman for the prophets, and this is a declaration of the inclusion of this third hypostasis in all the prophets. So you must make every prophet a compound of divinity and humanity, and that he is a complete God and a complete human being, as you said about Christ, since there is no difference between The indwellings of the Word and the indwellings of the Holy Spirit, both of them are hypostases.

Also, it is impossible for one of the two attributes to come without the other, and for the attribute to come without the Essence, so it is necessary for the living God to speak through His persons. The three are present in every prophet, and every prophet is the Lord of the worlds, and it is said with that: He is his son, and in this is great disbelief. The great contradiction is something that is not hidden, and this is absolutely necessary for the Christians, for what is proven for a thing is proven for its counterpart, and it is not permissible Differentiating between those who are similar, and they do not have the right to say: absolution or union in Christ is proven in the text, and there is no text in anything else, for reasons: one of which is:
The texts did not indicate any of that, as has become clear.
Second: That there are texts other than Christ that are similar to the texts contained in him, such as the word “the Son,” the word “descent of the Holy Spirit” in him, and the like.

Third: The evidence does not reflect, so the absence of specific evidence does not necessitate the absence of the signified, and not everything that God knew and honored His prophets with. He informed creation about it in a clear text, but among the connotations is the connotation of commitment.

If solutions and unity are proven in one of the two prophets in a common sense between him and the other prophet - it is necessary to reconcile those who are similar, as if It has been proven that a prophet should be believed because he is a prophet.
He declares the one who denies him a disbeliever because he is a prophet, so it follows that every prophet must be believed and the one who denies him a disbeliever.

Fourth: Suppose that there is no evidence to prove this in anything else, then it is necessary to permit this in something else. Since there is no evidence of its absence, as they say: This was established in Christ before he revealed the signs, as they say, and at that time So they are obligated to allow every prophet to be fully God and fully human like the Messiah, even if this is not known.
Fifth:

If that had not happened, it would have been permissible according to them, since there is no difference in God’s power between His union with Christ and His union with all other human beings. They must allow God to make every human being a complete God and a complete human being, and that every human being is a compound of divinity and humanity, and has drawn closer to This is the false conclusion of those who say that the souls of the children of Adam are from the essence of God, and that it is an ancient and eternal theology, so they make half of every human being Theology, and half of it is humanity, and these things require more impossibilities than the Christians require in some ways, and the impossibilities that require Christians are more, in some ways.

The second aspect: Their saying: If we say this, it does not oblige us to worship three gods, but rather one God, just as it does not oblige us if we say: Man, his soul, and his speech are three people, nor when we say: fire, its heat, and its light, three fires, nor when we say: the sun and its light. Its rays are three suns.

It is said: This is a false representation for several reasons: one of them is that the heat of fire and its light that flows through it is not fire from fire, nor a substance from another substance, nor He is equal in essence to fire and the sun, and the same is true of the word “man.” He is not a human being from another human being, nor is he equal to man in essence. Likewise, the sun, its light that flows through it, and its rays that flow through it - is neither a sun nor a subsisting substance by itself, and you said: He is a true God. From a true God, so you said about trustworthiness:

(We believe in one God, the Father, Almighty, and in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only Son of God, begotten of the Father before all ages, Light from Light, true God from true God, from the essence of His Father, equal in essence with the Father. And you said in the Holy Spirit: (He is a glorified Lord, worshiped. (His) So you established three lords.

The second: What is meant by the light in the sun and fire is the same light that is radiating from them, and what is meant by it is the ray that is radiating to the ground and the walls, and this Contrasting with it, not existing with it, and the word “light” expresses this and that, and both of them are an attribute that exists with something else and is an accident, and it may be meant by the word Light is the same as fire and the same as the sun and the moon.

So the light would be a self-subsisting essence, and if that were the case, then they made the Father a self-subsisting essence, and the Son also a self-subsisting Lord. Subsisting by Himself, and the Holy Spirit is Lord and Subsistence by Himself.

It is known that the light of fire, the sun, and its heat are not each of them a sun and fire subsisting on their own, nor a substance subsisting on their own. They affirmed the life of God and His knowledge or His words as two attributes related to Him, and they did not make this a Lord, an essence existing in Himself, and this a Lord, an essence. Existing in itself - their statement would have been true and their representation would have been identical, but they did not limit themselves to simply making them two attributes of God until they made both of them as Lord, substance, and Creator. Rather, they declared that Christ, with whom they claim one of them was united, is one God and Creator. If he were the same The word of God and His knowledge was not a creator god, for the word of God and His knowledge was not a creator god, so how come when Christ was created by the word of God, he was not The same Word of God?

The third aspect: That their saying: The sun, its rays, and its light, if they meant by light that which supports it, and by the rays that which is separated from it - This is not the example of fire, its heat, and its flame; Since they both do it, and based on this, the sun only did it in one capacity, not two, so the representation by it is not identical, even if They wanted both light and rays; What he does, or both; What is separate from it - they are both one attribute, they are not two attributes like life and knowledge, so it is known that representing them with the sun is a mistake. And some of them say:
The sun, its heat, and its light, as they say, is like that in hellfire.

This representation would be more correct if it were proven that there is heat in the body of the sun, because there is no evidence for this, and many wise people He denies it, and claims that the bodies of the sun, moon, and planets cannot be described as hot or cold, and this is the opinion of Aristotle and his followers.

As for their representation by the spirit of man and his speech, if they mean by the spirit his life, then this is not the concept of the spirit, and if they mean by the spirit that It departs from his body with death and is called the rational soul - this is a self-existent entity and is not one of its symptoms, and in that case it must be a soul. God is a substance existing by itself with another substance similar to the human body, and the Lord Glory be to Him is composed of a body and a soul like a human being, and is not This is the saying of the people of that religion, neither the Muslims, nor the Jews, nor the Christians. Rather, it is blasphemy according to them, so it became clear that their representation of the three Invalidity.

The fourth aspect: that representation occurs either with the attributes of the sun, fire, or man, or with the soul existing in these essences, or with what It is a contrast to that, such as the light that falls on the earth, walls, air, and other bodies when they encounter the sun, fire, or The human being or the soul that exists in these essences. If this is what is meant, then this is a reflected ray, an inverted light, and not an upright characteristic. With the sun and fire.

And if we mean what happened to this Messiah, this is called light and spirit, and it is called the light of God, as the Almighty said: {Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth, like His light. Like a niche in which there is a lamp. The lamp is in a bottle. The bottle is as if it were a pearly star, lit from a blessed tree, an olive neither of the east nor of A western land whose oil would almost shine even if no fire touched it. Light upon light. God guides to His light whomsoever He wills.} [An-Nur: 35].

And God Almighty said: {And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book or faith is, but We have made it a light by which We guide whom We will. Of Our servants} [Al-Shura: 52].
So He informed us that He made the spirit which He inspired into a light by which He guides whomsoever He wills.
And God Almighty said: {Those are He who wrote in their hearts faith and sustained them with a spirit from Him} [Al-Mujadila: 22].
And God Almighty said: {So those who believe in him and honor him and support him and follow the light that was sent down with him} [Al-A’raf: 157].
And God Almighty said: “And He makes for you a light by which you walk” [Al-Hadid: 28].
And the Almighty said: {And whoever does not assign light to him, then he has no light} [An-Nur: 40].

If what happened in Christ of the Spirit and the Word is meant in this sense, then Christ has no jurisdiction over that, for this is lawful in all The prophets and believers, even if they differed in it according to their degrees, and this situation in them is not the same as the characteristic of God that is present in it, even if it is That is due to it and caused by it, but it is not the same attribute of God, even if there are people who say: Rather, the attribute of God that He was characterized by is permissible. Concerning the servant, this statement is wrong, because the attribute of the being described cannot be performed in the same way by anyone else, but if a person Learn, teach

Someone else, and the words of someone else conveyed it. It is said: This is the knowledge of so-and-so and his words. Because this second one informed him about it, and what is meant is the knowledge of the first one and his words, with the knowledge that the same person who did the same thing as the first one is not him. It is the same as what the second did, even if it might be like it, and the first might be what is meant by the second, like someone who conveyed the words of others, so the words The informant is the one who is intended to inform.

The attributes of the conveyor - such as his movement and voice - through which the conveyor is conveyed; It is not the same as what is intended, and if these are said to be the words of the person being conveyed, the reference is to the truth of the words intended by the conveyance, not to what The one who communicates it is specific to it from his actions and attributes, and for this reason people likened those who say that the attribute of the Lord is permissible in His servant to Christians who say that it is permissible He is similar to them in some ways.

But Christians do not believe in the imposition of an abstract attribute, but rather in the imposition of the hypostasis, which is an essence characterized by the attribute, and they say: Christ is the Creator. And Raziq, and He is the creator of Adam and Mary, and He is the son of Adam and Mary, and He is their creator through His divinity and a son for them through His humanity.

They say: He is the Son of God, and He is God in His divinity. They also say in divinity and humanity for the sake of unity, and God has declared them unbelievers. By their saying: {Indeed, God is the Messiah, the son of Mary} [Al-Maeda: 17] and so on.

And if they wanted to represent them with the attributes of the sun, fire, and the soul, to represent them with what the sun, fire, and soul do of light and life. And speech, and they made what they affirm of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit - attributes of God, just as these are attributes of these creatures.

It was said to them first: None of the prophets, peace be upon them, expressed the attributes of God in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, so it is not yours then. You find in the words of Christ, peace be upon him, or other prophets, mention of faith in the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit - that you say: What they mean With that is the attribute of God, which is the word and knowledge, nor the life of God, as they did not want this meaning with this word, but rather they meant in the name The Son and the Holy Spirit are separate from God Almighty.

The one who separates from God is not an attribute of God, let alone the fact that He is the Creator, let alone the fact that mankind united with Him is a creator. You went astray after error, an error where you made the purpose of Christ and others the Son and the Holy Spirit - an attribute of the Lord, then a second error where you made the attribute Creator and Lord, then a third misguidance where you made the attribute unite with a human being, namely Jesus, and he is called the Messiah, and he is the Creator, Lord of the worlds, so you went astray in The solutions are a three-fold misguidance, after your misguidance in the Trinity also other misguidances, where you affirmed three attributes to the exclusion of others, and made them essences of lords, Then you said:
One God, so you have gone astray as a threefold error in the trinity, and a astray as a matter of threefold in the unity.
And it was said to you secondly:

If you make these attributes of God, just as light, sound, and heat are attributes of what they do - abstain from being replaced with something else, and abstain from being combined with The solutions are to be effective like fire, the sun, and the soul, and you have made the word and life a state other than God, and you have made what is permissible with it. He is a Creator God. Rather, He is the Creator God, and it is known that none of the wise people considers what happens in the light of fire a fire, nor what happens. In it there is a ray of the sun - a sun, and what takes place in it is Zayd’s speech and knowledge - it is the soul of Zayd, so your making the Messiah the Creator of the world is in contradiction to To represent you.

Thus it became clear that what you mentioned is not matched by any of the examples, as it was complete, false, contradictory and impossible to verify, so there is no representation With something of the fixed and known assets, unless it is an inconsistent representation.

For this reason they liken the solution and union sometimes to the dissolution of water into an envelope, and sometimes to the dissolution of fire into iron, and sometimes to the soul and body, and sometimes They say that they are one substance mixed together like water and milk are mixed, and all of these parables that they set forth for God are false parables. The water in the envelope and other containers needs its container. If its container were pierced, it would dissipate, while it is surrounded by it, and the envelope is not characterized by it. With any of the qualities of water, and the Almighty Lord refrains from needing any of His creatures, neither the Throne, nor anything else, or surrounding it. Something of existing things; Since He is the Manifest, there is nothing above Him.

It is also proven in the Sahih on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “You are the first, so there is nothing before you, and you are the last, so there is nothing after you.

And You are the Manifest, and nothing is above You, and You are the Inward, and there is nothing below You. For this reason, what God described Himself with was not similar to the attributes of created beings, just as His essence was not like the essence of created beings. He is equal to His throne, as He told us about Himself despite His need for the throne.

And the creature lying on a bed, ship, or animal, if what was under it were gone, it would fall; Because of his need for Him, and God is independent of everything else, and He is the One who supports the Throne and those who bear the Throne with His power.

The three groups of Christians say in unity, so it does not benefit them to imitate the solution of water in the circumstance, even if it is assumed that they said of the mere solution with The Lord does not need humanity. He does not contain it or touch it. Rather, just as He spoke to Moses from the tree, this necessitates that humanity is not characterized by any of The divine is like a tree,
Then it is necessarily known that the voice that was heard was the voice of humanity, so mutilating a tree is also invalid, as explained in its place.

As for iron, wood, and other things, if they are thrown into fire, they transform into fire because they come into contact with fire, not because the fire they transform into It was present, so it happened to him. This is an impossibility without a solution, and the fire that became in the iron was caused by that fire, not it. Then If that iron is struck, it is as if it were struck on fire, and likewise if it is thrown into water, if this were an identical representation, the striking would be The crucifixion and humiliation occurred on the Divinity, and the Divinity was the one who washes with water, and the one who eats and drinks, and this is one of the greatest Disbelief.

It is said about some of them, such as the Jacobites, that they speak of this disbelief, even though many of them, such as the Melkites and Nestorians, are He denies it, for it is necessary for them. Likewise, if they liken it to the soul and the body, then the soul suffers as the body suffers, and its attributes become impossible. By being in the body, and acquiring morals and attributes from the body, if this were an identical representation, divinity would have to suffer through the pain of the body. And that he should be suffering from bodily hunger, thirst, beatings, and crucifixion, and that he should be in distress due to what he has acquired of the characteristics of the humanity that he is. To them, it is in the same position as the body is to the soul, and as for their saying:

Since we did not neglect what we received, nor did we reject what we imitated, their saying in this matter is like the Jews saying to Christ: We do not neglect what We received it, and we do not reject what we learned from Moses, peace be upon him.

The response of the two sects comes from two aspects: One of them: That you have altered and distorted the Book that was revealed to you, and the law that was legislated for you, and you changed Meanings and rulings There is no doubt about it among all rational people, and what the Jews were following after the change was not the law that Moses legislated. Peace be upon him, and what the Christians followed after the change was not the law that Christ, peace be upon him, legislated.

The second: That you have denied the other Book, and the other Messenger that was sent to you, and whoever denies what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and the Messenger who He was sent to him - he was an unbeliever deserving of the punishment of this world and the hereafter, and if before that he had followed the law of a messenger and a book that had not been changed, so how? If it had been changed, would its provisions and meanings have been changed?

chapters.title: Chapter: Dropping their argument with something from the Qur’an once again based on their falsehood and that the entire Qur’an is taken away
paragraphs: [Chapter: Once again, their argument for something from the Qur’an is based on their falsehood and that the entire Qur’an will be taken away.]
As for their saying: We have these testimonies and evidence from the book that is in the hands of these people.

It is said: It is not valid for them to cite this book and provide evidence in any way, for what he brought with it has been transmitted from it. He was told that he was sent to them, and that they are infidels if they do not believe in him, deserving of jihad, and whoever does not consider their jihad permissible So he is an unbeliever, and the Qur’an is full of their disbelief. So if this is a messenger from God, and he informed of their disbelief; It is proven that they are infidels.

The Messenger does not say anything about God except the truth. He does not lie about God about anything, and whoever lies about God, even in a single word, is one of the liars. Those who invent lies about God are deserving of the punishment of liars, as God Almighty said: {Even if he uttered some words against us} [Al-Haqqah: 44] (44) {We would certainly have taken from him by the right hand} [Al-Haqqah: 45] (45) {Then We would have severed from him the two jaws} [Al-Haqqah: 46] (46) {And there is not one of you who can withhold from him} [Al-Haqqah: 47].
{Or do they say, “He has invented a lie against God? Then if God wills, He will seal your heart, and God will erase falsehood and establish the truth with His words.” [Al-Shura: 24]

And God Almighty said: {And when We substitute a verse in place of another, and God knows best what He is sending down, they say, “Indeed, you are an inventor.” Nay, most of them do not know.} [An-Nahl: 101] (101) {Say, “It has been sent down by the Holy Spirit from your Lord with the truth, that He may confirm those who believe, and as guidance and good news for the Muslims.” [An-Nahl: 102].

And God Almighty said: {And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not hope for the meeting with Us say, “Bring a Qur’an other than this, or alter it.” Say, “It is not for me.” That I should change it of my own accord, that I should follow only what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a grievous Day.} [Yunus: 15] (15) {Say, “If He had willed.” By God, I did not recite it to you, nor did I make it known to you. I had remained among you for a lifetime before it. Will you not understand?} [Yunus: 16]

So whenever a word of this book is a lie against God, it is not the Book of God, and it was not brought by the Messenger of God, for the liar has He is truthful in most of what he says, but if he lies in some of what he says then he is a liar, and God Almighty does not send someone who lies to him. A created being does not want to send someone whom he knows is lying to him, and if he did that it would indicate his ignorance or inability, so how could he send the Lord? The knowledgeable is the one who knows that he is being lied to.

Then, when they deny a single word in the Book, their quoting and reasoning with anything in the Book is not valid, even if If they believe in the Book in its entirety, they must believe in what it brings, follow its law, and acknowledge the disbelief of those who deny it, and the disbelief of those who say: God is the Messiah, the son of Mary, and God is the third of three.

This is in contrast to the one who believed in the Messenger, and for whom some of what was reported from him was not proven or did not know its meaning, for this does not undermine the foundation of His faith in the Messenger.
If Muslims deny some of what was transmitted from Moses and Christ, then it is because they are attacking the transmitter, not the Prophet from whom it was transmitted.

As for the Christians, they know that Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, came with the Qur’an, so they criticized some of it as they criticized the Messenger himself and disbelieved in it. This is not the same as what they represented from the document whose payment was written on the back, for the one who owed the debt acknowledged the payment. The one who dropped it for him, there is no right left for him to claim, other than what he tells him who says: He is the Messenger of God, for he says:

God has sent down this entire book to me, and sent me with such-and-such to such-and-such. If he lies in anything of what he was told about God, It was not God who sent him, for the one who sent him is the one who made him convey what he said, without addition or subtraction, and God’s sending of the Messenger It includes two things:
God created the message, and God is Wise, and He knows best where He places His messages. He only places them among those who are among the most perfect of creation. And I believe them.

It includes God informing him that He has spoken the truth about him, as He informs him of what he says: God sent him with it, just as He has confirmed it with the signs. The miracles in his saying: He sent me, so he believed what he said: He sent me with it, since he believed that he sent him without knowledge. Because he is truthful in what he tells - there is no benefit in it, and the purpose of the message is not achieved.

And God Almighty is All-Knowing of what He testifies to whom He sent, unlike the creature who sends someone whom he thinks is truthful in what he informs him of. So it appears that he was lied to, and God knows the consequences of matters, and the message came from his knowledge and wisdom, and He is All-Knowing, All-Wise. He lies about God, even if it is in a word that does not convey what he says about him. In this manner, he is not His messenger.

For this reason, the people of religion agreed that the messengers are infallible in what they convey about God. They do not lie to Him intentionally or by mistake. This is The intent of the message, so representing this in the document was false, as the one claiming omission did not claim contradictory statements, but rather said: I decided This debt, then I paid it to you, and you acknowledge its fulfillment, and your acknowledgment is written on the back, so you have no right to use my declaration as evidence. The debt without your acknowledgment of repayment. Rather, you either consider what is in the document of my acknowledgment and yours, or you nullify both matters. The opposing parties.

This is a just statement, as two negotiating partners, such as a free rein partner, say to its owner: If a profit occurs, it is for me and for you, and if not, If there is a profit, it is neither mine nor yours.

Likewise, the seller and the lessor who say: If there is a bargain between us, then you have to hand over what you paid for, and I have to hand over what you paid for, is not worthy of Except for this, for all of this is fair and just speech, unlike the person in which it is said: He is the Messenger of God, and the book in which it is said:

It is the word of God, and God sent it down, for if this is a truthful messenger, then everything that has been conveyed to him from God is true, and if he is a liar then it is not God sent him, so everything he reported on the authority of God is a lie against God. It is not permissible, just because of his information, to attribute anything to God and not use what he informs as evidence. On the authority of God for something.

Don't you see that someone who claims the message and knows that he is a liar is like Al-Aswad Al-'Ansi, Musaylamah Al-Kadhab, Tulayha Al-Asadi, and Al-Harith Al-Dimashqi, And Baba Al-Rumi, and others - it is not permissible for anyone to use as evidence anything of what they mentioned that God sent them with, even if that is what they say. He knew that it was true on the other hand, because he knew that it was a lie that God did not send them, so what did they say that God sent down to them? They were lying about it, and once it is known that he is lying about the same specific news, it is not permissible to use as evidence the type of thing about which it is known that he lied.

Likewise, if a man with me said: Moses, David, or the Messiah (they lied about God about some of what they reported about God, they would be in the same position) Those to whom God did not send anything, but they lied in their saying that God sent them, then if he wanted, in addition to this, to use as evidence what was transmitted from The Torah, the Psalms, and the Gospel from God were contradictory, and his protest was invalid and unacceptable. Rather, if he had said: I doubt some of They told it about God. Did they lie about it or not?
He was also in doubt that God had sent them, for whoever God has sent does not lie about anything, whether by mistake or intentionally, and despite his doubt in

That is why it is not permissible to use anything of what they narrate from God as evidence to allow them to be liars about what they narrated from God. This is not like the Messenger of one of the human beings, for he may have sent him, and then the Messenger was truthful in some of what was conveyed to him by his sender. And he lied about some.
It is permissible for a human being to send someone who is lying to him due to his lack of knowledge of his lie, or his lack of wisdom in sending him.
As for the Lord Almighty:

It is not permissible for him to send a prophet who will lie to him, whether intentionally or by mistake. Likewise, the witness and the informant who know that sometimes he is truthful and sometimes true. He lies - some of his reports in which his truthfulness appears to be evidence can be used as evidence associated with that, unlike the Messenger, for if He lied one lie, denying that God had sent him, so everything he reported about God was false in that God sent him with it. So his lying about one word necessitates that he is a liar about everything he reported about God, and that everything he told and narrated about God is a lie about him. Even if it is assumed that those words in themselves are true, but his reporting about God, his transmission, his narration, and his story about God are a lie to God.

God has told us that He abrogates what Satan delivers, which contradicts the purpose of conveying the message, in the Almighty’s saying: {And We did not send before you Messenger or prophet, unless he makes a wish. Satan makes his wish, so God cancels what Satan makes. Then God establishes His signs, and God is All-Knowing. Wise} [Al-Hajj: 52] (52) {That He may make what Satan casts a test for those in whose hearts is sickness and whose hearts are hardened. And indeed, the wrongdoers are in far-off discord.} [Hajj:

53] (53) {And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, and believe in it, so that their hearts are humbled before Him. Indeed, God is the Guide of those who believe to A straight path} [Al-Hajj: 54] (54) {And those who disbelieve will remain in doubt about it until the Hour comes to them suddenly or the torment of a destructive Day comes to them.} [Al-Hajj: 55]

And if they say: His reports contradict each other, the answer is from two sides: One of them: This too, if it is true, then it casts doubt on His message, for the Messenger does not contradict one another in his information, and if that is the case then it is not right for you to use anything of what he brought as evidence. If it is false, it will not be rejected.

So it is known that their inference based on what is in this book on the validity of their religion, with which they violated this book - is extremely corrupt, and it is a combination of The two opposites and an inference from what is in the Book, which necessitates the invalidity of inference with something in the Book.
