If the result requires that some of the premises of the evidence are invalid, then the inference based on that evidence is invalid, which is only valid if its premises are correct. If its premise is only valid if its conclusion is invalid, and its conclusion necessitates the invalidity of its premise - then the combination of the validity of the premise, The result is a combination of the two opposites.

Likewise, whoever uses something from the Book as evidence that contradicts what is in the Book, such as Christians using verses in it as evidence for the validity of their religion, that is a contradiction. If this evidence is correct, then praising their religion while criticizing it would be contradictory, and a contradictory book is not the Book of God.

And if one of them becomes corrupted, either their religion is corrupted, or his praise is corrupted, then the book in which there is corruption is not the Book of God, so it must not be The Book of God is according to the two decrees, so it is not valid to infer it from the standpoint of the fact that it is God’s news, but as for inference from it from the standpoint of the fact that The speaker is a knowledgeable and wise man, and this does not benefit knowledge, as no one is infallible except the prophets, peace be upon them.

The Christians allow it to be infallible other than the prophets, so assuming that it is so is proof against them, even if they say: He is a man. A scholar is not a messenger from God. It was said to them that this statement of his is not an argument for the permissibility of him making a mistake, but his statement is to be relied upon. But if he claims that God sent him, but He did not send him with this entire book - so this is a liar, none of what he says can be used as evidence, and such a thing cannot be just and virtuous. About being wise, but rather he is one of those who invent a lie against God:
“And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God or says, ‘It has been revealed to me,’ but nothing was revealed to him.” [Al-An’am: 93].
The second answer: We have shown that what they mentioned does not contradict anything of what was reported, and that there is no contradiction in this book that they protest. In one way or another.
As for their saying: Our greatest proof is the testimony we found in it that God has placed us above those who disbelieved until the Day of Resurrection.

It is said: Rather, what they mentioned is a proof against them and not for them. For God told Christ that He would place those who followed Him above those who disbelieved until the Day of Judgment. Resurrection, and the news of God is true, and the promise of God is true, and God does not break His promise, so when those who believed in Him followed Christ, God placed them above those The Jews and others disbelieved in him.

Then when God sent Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, with the religion with which he sent Christ and all the prophets before him, and Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was And he greeted, confirming what the Messiah brought, and the Messiah was bringing good news of a messenger whose name would come after him (Ahmed). The nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, became And peace be upon the Christians who followed Christ, peace be upon him, who changed his law and denied him in what he preached, so God made the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he will be raised above the Christians until the Day of Resurrection.

He also made them above the Jews until the Day of Resurrection, and the Christians, after abrogation and alteration, are not followers of Christ, but they are following Him. Among the Jews who went to extremes in denying him and insulting him, for they denied him first, and they denied Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, secondly, so they became more distant from About the Christians following Christ, so they were superior to the Jews.

The believers are the nation of Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, they are the followers of Christ, peace be upon him, and whoever other than them disbelieves in him is the nation of Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. He was above the Jews and Christians until the Day of Resurrection, and for this reason, when the Muslims came to fight the Christians, they defeated them and took from them The choice of land: the Holy Land, and the surrounding areas of Egypt and the peninsula, and the land of the West. The Muslims were still victorious over the Christians. And they will continue until the Day of Resurrection. The Christians have never been victorious over all Muslims.
It only defeats a group of Muslims because of their sins, and then God supports the believers over them.

If the Christians were the followers of Christ, peace be upon him, and the Muslims were disbelievers in him - it would be necessary for them to be victorious over all Muslims. Because all Muslims deny the divinity of Christ and consider Christians unbelievers, so it is known that those who follow Christ are the Muslims, not the Christians.
